news.originalContent:
در پی کشته‌شدن دو سرباز ارتش اسرائيل در شهر الخلیل در کرانه باختری اشغالی، اسرائیل عملیات امنیتی گسترده را در این شهر آغاز کرده و بنیامین نتانیاهو، نخست‌وزیر، از«یک غافلگیری بسیار بزرگ تشکیلات فلسطینی» صحبت کرده است.

این دو سرباز روز جمعه (اول آبان) با تیراندازی دو فلسطینی مجروح شدند و بعد بر اثر شدت جراحات، جان باختند. این دو فلسطینی نیز همان وقت به ضرب گلوله سربازان اسرائیل کشته شدند.

ارتش اسرائیل همچنین گفته است که این عملیات، منطقه‌ای از الخلیل را هدف قرار داده که دو مهاجم مسلح فلسطینی از آنجا آمده بودند و ممکن است چندین روز به طول انجامد.

بنیامین نتانیاهو، نخست‌وزیر اسرائیل، نیز وعده داد محله‌ای را که این مهاجمان از آنجا آمده بودند، ویران کند. او گفت: «گام اول شامل آواره کردن ساکنان، تفتیش خانه‌ها و نابودی زیرساخت‌های تروریستی خواهد بود.»

منابع محلی می‌گویند از روز گذشته دست‌کم ۲۵۰ خانواده به‌اجبار از خانه‌های خود در این شهر بیرون رانده شده‌اند.

خبرگزاری فرانسه گزارش داد که در محله «عین دیر بها» که میان دو تپه واقع شده است، روی ساختمان‌های تخلیه شده علامت ضربدر دیده می‌شود.

در این گزارش آمده که خیابان‌های این منطقه از مردم و خودروها تخلیه شده و تنها چند خودروی نظامی اسرائیلی در آنجا به چشم می‌خورد.

به برخی ساکنان و فروشندگان محلی دو ساعت فرصت داده شد تا محل زندگی و کسب خود را ترک کنند.

خالد دودین، فرماندار الخلیل، به خبرگزاری فرانسه گفت که حدود یک‌سوم این شهر هدف عملیات ارتش اسرائيل قرار گرفته است.

او گفت: «آن‌ها کار را از محله‌ای آغاز کردند که عاملان حمله از آنجا آمده بودند، اما هیچ تضمینی وجود ندارد که دامنه این عملیات گسترش نیابد.»

آقای دودین افزود: «این اقدام در حکم مجازات دسته‌جمعی غیرنظامیانی است که هیچ‌گونه ارتباطی با این ماجرا ندارند.»

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

بنیامین نتانیاهو اما می‌گوید که «اقدامات بزرگ‌تری» در راه است.

او در مصاحبه‌ای با شبکه آی۲۴ نیوز که شامگاه جمعه انجام شد، درباره تشکیلات فلسطینی گفت: «من برای خنثی کردن این تهدید، از روش‌هایی استفاده خواهم کرد که به نظرم بهتر است فعلاً جزئیات آن را فاش نکنم.»

نخست‌وزیر اسرائيل همچنین در پاسخ به این سوال که آیا با انحلال تشکیلات فلسطینی موافق است یا نه، گفت که در گذشته در برابر فشار سه رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا برای تلاش در جهت تشکیل یک کشور فلسطینی ایستادگی کرده است.

ایتامار بن‌گویر، مشاور امنیت ملی اسرائيل، که از چهره‌های راست افراطی این کشور محسوب می‌شود از دولت خواسته تا تشکیلات فلسطینی را منحل کند. محبوبیت او در نظرسنجی‌های پیش از انتخابات سه‌شنبه آتی رو به افزایش است.

این در حالی است که تا این لحظه، هیچ مدرکی برای دخالت تشکیلات فلسطینی در حمله الخلیل پیدا نشده است.

آقای نتانیاهو در این مصاحبه با اشاره به حملات اسرائيل به غزه، لبنان، سوریه و ایران گفت: «ما خاورمیانه را دگرگون کردیم. من گفته بودم که اوضاع را تغییر خواهیم داد و همین کار را هم کردیم.»

او افزود: «یک غافلگیری بسیار بزرگ هم برای تشکیلات فلسطینی در کار است.»

این در حالی است که ساعتی پس از انتشار اخبار این حادثه،‌ حماس از حمله به سربازان اسرائيلی استقبال کرد و از فلسطینیان خواست تا حملات بیشتری انجام دهند. با این حال حماس رسما مسئولیت این حمله را بر عهده نگرفت.

این حمله پس از افزایش تنش‌ها در کرانه باختری رخ داد. شهرک‌نشینان اسرائیلی، که از حمایت قوی متحدان راست افراطی نتانیاهو برخوردارند، تصرف زمین‌های فلسطینی و حملات به آنها را افزایش داده‌اند.

گروه حقوق بشری یش دین، ۶۷۲ مورد خشونت شهرک‌نشینان را در ۲۶ روز گذشته گزارش داده که تقریباً نیمی از آنها مربوط به برداشت زیتون است؛ یک رویداد فرهنگی سالانه برای فلسطینی‌ها که شهرک‌نشینان افراطی به دنبال توقف آن بوده‌اند.

تشکیلات فلسطینی، نهادی خودگردان است که بر اساس توافق‌های صلح دهه ۱۹۹۰، با همکاری اسرائیل بر بخش‌هایی از کرانه باختری حکومت می‌کند.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by JONNE RORIZ/AFP via Getty Images)

Attorneys and self-defense instructors told the Daily Caller News Foundation that firing a warning shot is almost a surefire way to face legal trouble, assuming one survives the incident.

In two recent incidents armed citizens fired warning shots, with one in Benton County, Washington, jailed on suspicion of murder for a few days while the police investigated until the prosecutor admitted the shooting was actually self-defense. In the second incident in Franklin County, Missouri, police filed no charges against the armed citizen, but experts warn that those who advise firing warning shots are missing the mark.

“Warning shots are generally forbidden for police and strongly recommended against for private citizens. There are often more earwitnesses than eyewitnesses, and they may interpret ‘Stop or I’ll shoot’ followed by a BANG as ‘He threatened to shoot someone, then carried out the threat,’” Second Amendment Foundation President Massad Ayoob, an expert witness and instructor in the use of force, told the DCNF. “The suspect in question may claim that the warning shot was a murder attempt and the shooter simply missed.” (RELATED: Blue State Prosecutor Admits Man Arrested For Murder Actually Acted In Self-Defense)

“Also, the bullet has to go somewhere,” Ayoob continued. “In one case, an officer in a city fired a warning shot upward to halt a felon running away from him, and the bullet struck and killed an innocent citizen on the top floor porch of a tenement building. To put the bullet somewhere safe, the shooter has to take his eyes off a potentially dangerous suspect. There are many downsides to firing warning shots.”

United States Concealed Carry Association (USCCA) principal training advisor Rob Chadwick agreed, warning that the use of warning shots could lead to trouble in court.

What feels like the safest choice in a moment of crisis often becomes the biggest trap in court. #warningshot #USLawShield #SelfDefense #LegalDefense #2A https://t.co/l1oZaW7UUv

“Firing a warning shot means discharging a deadly weapon without stopping the threat. Instructors teach that every round needs an identified target and a safe backstop,” Chadwick told the DCNF. “Laws on warning shots and self-defense vary by state, but in any jurisdiction a warning shot invites prosecutors to argue the shooter never faced the level of danger that justifies deadly force.”

Marc Victor, owner of Attorneys For Freedom Law Firm, said after trying “thousands” of cases, he viewed warning shots as “high risk” in the legal aftermath of a self-defense incident.

“Prosecutors like to use them really in a couple of different ways. First, if you’re firing a warning shot, lots of prosecutors will make the argument that because you had the ability to fire a warning shot the whole situation was not imminent,” Victor told the DCNF. “As imminency is a very important piece of building a self-defense case the prosecutor very commonly in these types of cases will say, because you had time to fire a warning shot, you were not at an imminent threat of death or serious physical injury. The reason I say it that way is because when you fire a warning shot you’re now in the category of deadly physical force.”

“You’re going to have to make the case that you are at an imminent risk of death or a very serious physical injury, and so they will use the warning shot as their evidence that the imminency card was missing, so that’s number one,” Victor continued. “The second thing that we see commonly on warning shots is a prosecutor will argue this was an escalation. You weren’t trying to use the least amount of force, what escalated the situation. So now you’re the aggressor, you’re not responding to the aggression.”

Even in a situation where nobody was struck by the bullet, Victor noted that prosecutors could still charge a gun owner who fired a warning shot in a self-defense situation.

“You are going to be responsible for where that round lands, and so it’s very common people get charged with unlawful discharge or endangerment because the prosecutor is going to make the case that you recklessly endangered other people by firing a shot up into the air,” Victor told the DCNF. “That round is going to come back down. You could even get charged with an aggravated assault. So another reason to discourage warning shots is because innocent bystanders sometimes get hit. You’re definitely going to be charged with a crime in that circumstance.”

Tom Grieve, an attorney affiliated with the United States Concealed Carry Association, noted that the warning shots could actually hand an edge to a criminal who assaulted an armed citizen.

“I want you to think of a defensive gun use as two deadly events unfolding at once: the kinetic encounter with your attacker and then the legal encounter that follows. Both the man in the mask demanding your property or your life and the justice system can ruin and take everything you have. That makes them both deadly force encounters,” Grieve told the DCNF. “Warning shots end attacks in the street but begin attacks against your future in court. Every case my firm has seen where someone contacted our office after using warning shots faced criminal charges after the bad guys fled. The reasoning? It’s a circular logic.” (RELATED: Bizarre Shovel Attack Over Porch-Peeing Dispute Ends With Gunshot)

“You are privileged to use deadly force, such as discharging a firearm, only if you are facing a deadly threat. The specifics vary from place and time, but that’s the short version. A prosecutor will ask: Was it really an imminent deadly threat if you could risk a warning shot instead of directly shooting the attacker?” Grieve continued. “If the warning shot fails to stop the attack, you may be dead. Alternatively, it was never a deadly threat to the point where deadly force was justified, meaning you jumped the shark, so enjoy these felony charges. Typical charges range from recklessly endangering safety, attempted homicide, to intentionally pointing a firearm.”

Grieve also cautioned that assailants would often try to claim they were the victim in the incident.

“By the way: every time the police interview the bad guys they 90% of the time claim that you attacked them. Remember, these assailants did not just wake up one day, decide to skip going to their W2 job and figure they will wing it [and] try some violent street felonies,” Grieve said. “It’s usually a long road to committing violent street felonies. They and their best friends have been arrested and in and out of the system for already many years. These bad guys know the system and they know how to play the cops. It does not always work out for them, but it does a frightening amount of the time because the good guys (that’s you, the victim) do not understand the system and what you are up against.”

Under current federal law, those convicted of an offense that can lead to more than one year in prison or those under indictment for such an offense are prohibited from possessing firearms.

In two recent incidents armed citizens fired warning shots, with one in Benton County, Washington, jailed on suspicion of murder for a few days while the police investigated until the prosecutor admitted the shooting was actually self-defense. In the second incident in Franklin County, Missouri, police filed no charges against the armed citizen, but experts warn that those who advise firing warning shots are missing the mark.

“Warning shots are generally forbidden for police and strongly recommended against for private citizens. There are often more earwitnesses than eyewitnesses, and they may interpret ‘Stop or I’ll shoot’ followed by a BANG as ‘He threatened to shoot someone, then carried out the threat,’” Second Amendment Foundation President Massad Ayoob, an expert witness and instructor in the use of force, told the DCNF. “The suspect in question may claim that the warning shot was a murder attempt and the shooter simply missed.” (RELATED: Blue State Prosecutor Admits Man Arrested For Murder Actually Acted In Self-Defense)

“Also, the bullet has to go somewhere,” Ayoob continued. “In one case, an officer in a city fired a warning shot upward to halt a felon running away from him, and the bullet struck and killed an innocent citizen on the top floor porch of a tenement building. To put the bullet somewhere safe, the shooter has to take his eyes off a potentially dangerous suspect. There are many downsides to firing warning shots.”

United States Concealed Carry Association (USCCA) principal training advisor Rob Chadwick agreed, warning that the use of warning shots could lead to trouble in court.

What feels like the safest choice in a moment of crisis often becomes the biggest trap in court. #warningshot #USLawShield #SelfDefense #LegalDefense #2A https://t.co/l1oZaW7UUv

“Firing a warning shot means discharging a deadly weapon without stopping the threat. Instructors teach that every round needs an identified target and a safe backstop,” Chadwick told the DCNF. “Laws on warning shots and self-defense vary by state, but in any jurisdiction a warning shot invites prosecutors to argue the shooter never faced the level of danger that justifies deadly force.”

Marc Victor, owner of Attorneys For Freedom Law Firm, said after trying “thousands” of cases, he viewed warning shots as “high risk” in the legal aftermath of a self-defense incident.

“Prosecutors like to use them really in a couple of different ways. First, if you’re firing a warning shot, lots of prosecutors will make the argument that because you had the ability to fire a warning shot the whole situation was not imminent,” Victor told the DCNF. “As imminency is a very important piece of building a self-defense case the prosecutor very commonly in these types of cases will say, because you had time to fire a warning shot, you were not at an imminent threat of death or serious physical injury. The reason I say it that way is because when you fire a warning shot you’re now in the category of deadly physical force.”

“You’re going to have to make the case that you are at an imminent risk of death or a very serious physical injury, and so they will use the warning shot as their evidence that the imminency card was missing, so that’s number one,” Victor continued. “The second thing that we see commonly on warning shots is a prosecutor will argue this was an escalation. You weren’t trying to use the least amount of force, what escalated the situation. So now you’re the aggressor, you’re not responding to the aggression.”

Even in a situation where nobody was struck by the bullet, Victor noted that prosecutors could still charge a gun owner who fired a warning shot in a self-defense situation.

“You are going to be responsible for where that round lands, and so it’s very common people get charged with unlawful discharge or endangerment because the prosecutor is going to make the case that you recklessly endangered other people by firing a shot up into the air,” Victor told the DCNF. “That round is going to come back down. You could even get charged with an aggravated assault. So another reason to discourage warning shots is because innocent bystanders sometimes get hit. You’re definitely going to be charged with a crime in that circumstance.”

Tom Grieve, an attorney affiliated with the United States Concealed Carry Association, noted that the warning shots could actually hand an edge to a criminal who assaulted an armed citizen.

“I want you to think of a defensive gun use as two deadly events unfolding at once: the kinetic encounter with your attacker and then the legal encounter that follows. Both the man in the mask demanding your property or your life and the justice system can ruin and take everything you have. That makes them both deadly force encounters,” Grieve told the DCNF. “Warning shots end attacks in the street but begin attacks against your future in court. Every case my firm has seen where someone contacted our office after using warning shots faced criminal charges after the bad guys fled. The reasoning? It’s a circular logic.” (RELATED: Bizarre Shovel Attack Over Porch-Peeing Dispute Ends With Gunshot)

“You are privileged to use deadly force, such as discharging a firearm, only if you are facing a deadly threat. The specifics vary from place and time, but that’s the short version. A prosecutor will ask: Was it really an imminent deadly threat if you could risk a warning shot instead of directly shooting the attacker?” Grieve continued. “If the warning shot fails to stop the attack, you may be dead. Alternatively, it was never a deadly threat to the point where deadly force was justified, meaning you jumped the shark, so enjoy these felony charges. Typical charges range from recklessly endangering safety, attempted homicide, to intentionally pointing a firearm.”

Grieve also cautioned that assailants would often try to claim they were the victim in the incident.

“By the way: every time the police interview the bad guys they 90% of the time claim that you attacked them. Remember, these assailants did not just wake up one day, decide to skip going to their W2 job and figure they will wing it [and] try some violent street felonies,” Grieve said. “It’s usually a long road to committing violent street felonies. They and their best friends have been arrested and in and out of the system for already many years. These bad guys know the system and they know how to play the cops. It does not always work out for them, but it does a frightening amount of the time because the good guys (that’s you, the victim) do not understand the system and what you are up against.”

Under current federal law, those convicted of an offense that can lead to more than one year in prison or those under indictment for such an offense are prohibited from possessing firearms.

news.originalContent:
(Getty Images/Gent Shkullaku)

Military boards are disobeying Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s ban on openly transgender-identifying service members in the U.S. Armed Forces.

Nine of 12 Navy and Marine Corps review boards have recommended retaining transgender service members despite Pentagon directives calling for their discharge, according to The New York Times. The decisions raise questions about enforcement of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s military personnel policies and whether individual review boards are prioritizing their own ideology over the Pentagon’s stated readiness standards. (RELATED: Troy Jackson Backed Trans Prison Policy — Female Inmate Says Convicted Killer Threatened To Rape Her)

Directly after this executive order, the Pentagon enacted a system paying transgender service members to voluntarily separate from the military, the Times reported. As a result, hundreds left.

Those who challenged their dismissal faced three-member separation boards, according to the outlet. Those officers were given a set of criteria that a service member must meet to be dismissed. Boards of sailors and Marines have completely disregarded the criteria.

The Pentagon told the Daily Caller News Foundation that it does not comment on ongoing litigation.

“The Armed Forces have been afflicted with radical gender ideology to appease activists unconcerned with the requirements of military service like physical and mental health, selflessness, and unit cohesion,” President Donald Trump Stated in a January 2025 Executive Order. “[E]xpressing a false ‘gender identity’ divergent from an individual’s sex cannot satisfy the rigorous standards necessary for military service … adoption of a gender identity inconsistent with an individual’s sex conflicts with a soldier’s commitment to an honorable, truthful, and disciplined lifestyle, even in one’s personal life. A man’s assertion that he is a woman, and his requirement that others honor this falsehood, is not consistent with the humility and selflessness required of a service member.”

The U.S. Military is gender neutral and merit based. If you need to identify as anything other than male or female which is what the paperwork across the nation usually has in its infrastructure, then you disqualify yourself. Many were also joining the military to get their transgender surgeries and treatments paid for by the federal government. The military should not be the personal elective treatment facility for anyone. That was a waste of the military’s time and money. If you want surgery, stay out of the military and pay for it yourself like you should.

Marine Staff Sgt. Damien Contreras, a biological female, was put on paid leave in April due to a 2017 sex change hormone usage and her choice to identify as a male, according to the Times. In August, she was flown from Hawaii to Marine Corps Base Quantico to face a separation board. At the hearing, a government lawyer presented documents proving her struggles with gender identity. Rather than circle “a history of cross sex hormone therapy,” automatic grounds for separation, they circled “remains qualified.”

The Navy has nearly twice as many people who identify as gay, bisexual or transgender compared to other branches which indicated potential ideological bias, the Times reported.

اکسیوس از یک هشدار اطلاعاتی آمریکا درباره طرح‌های احتمالی ایران برای ترور مقام‌های آمریکایی خبر داده و سی‌ان‌ان گزارش کرده که دولت آمریکا بی‌سروصدا در حال کاهش شمار دیپلمات‌ها و خانواده‌های آنان در چند کشور خاورمیانه است.

news.originalContent:
در حالی که دونالد ترامپ بار دیگر از احتمال حمله نظامی به ایران سخن گفته است، گزارش‌های تازه رسانه‌های آمریکایی از افزایش نگرانی واشنگتن درباره پیامدهای دور جدید جنگ حکایت دارند.

اکسیوس از یک هشدار اطلاعاتی آمریکا درباره طرح‌های احتمالی ایران برای ترور مقام‌های آمریکایی خبر داده و سی‌ان‌ان گزارش کرده که دولت آمریکا بی‌سروصدا در حال کاهش شمار دیپلمات‌ها و خانواده‌های آنان در چند کشور خاورمیانه است.

وال‌استریت ژورنال در دو گزارش جداگانه از تهدید ایران به حمله به زیرساخت‌های اقتصادی منطقه و تلاش آمریکا برای محدود کردن آخرین مسیرهای تجارت زمینی ایران خبر داده است؛ فشاری که با بسته شدن برخی گذرگاه‌های مرزی عراق و پاکستان شدت گرفته است.

در این میان، سخنان سفیر آمریکا در سازمان ملل درباره احتمال ادامه جنگ تا یک سال دیگر، با تأکید ترامپ بر امکان پایان سریع درگیری، تصویری از ابهام در راهبرد واشنگتن ارائه می‌دهد.

در این مطلب بعضی از مطالب مربوط به جنگ ایران که جمعه در رسانه های آمریکا منتشر شدند،‌ مرور می‌شوند.

اکسیوس به یک یادداشت اطلاعاتی یک‌صفحه‌ای به تاریخ ۲۳ اکتبر دست یافته است که بر اساس آن، دستگاه‌های اطلاعاتی آمریکا معتقدند ایران تلاش‌های خود برای هدف قرار دادن دیپلمات‌ها و مقام‌های آمریکایی در خاورمیانه و دیگر نقاط جهان را به‌شدت افزایش داده است.

در این یادداشت که جی کلیتون، مدیر اطلاعات ملی آمریکا، برای مارکو روبیو، وزیر خارجه، فرستاده، ادعا شده که برخی طرح‌های احتمالی برای کشتن مقام‌های آمریکایی به مراحل پیشرفته رسیده‌اند. با این حال، این سند هویت افراد مورد تهدید، کشورهای مشخص خارج از خاورمیانه یا جزئیات عملیاتی این طرح‌ها را فاش نمی‌کند.

آقای کلیتون همچنین هشدار داده است که اطلاعات موجود درباره این تهدیدها باید در اختیار شمار بیشتری از کارکنان دولت آمریکا قرار گیرد. او پیشنهاد کرده بخشی از اطلاعات حساس با سطح محرمانگی پایین‌تری در اختیار افرادی قرار گیرد که احتمالاً در معرض خطر هستند.

به گفته یک مقام آمریکایی، نگرانی درباره این طرح‌های ادعایی، در کنار افزایش حملات حوثی‌های یمن، از دلایل تصمیم وزارت خارجه برای کاهش حضور کارکنان در سفارتخانه‌های آمریکا در امارات متحده عربی، قطر، اردن و لبنان بوده است.

پیش‌تر نیز به کارکنان غیرضروری و خانواده‌های کارکنان دیپلماتیک آمریکا در عربستان سعودی دستور خروج داده شده بود.

این هشدار در حالی منتشر شده که دونالد ترامپ روز جمعه در یک گردهمایی انتخاباتی در فلوریدا بار دیگر احتمال اجرای عملیاتی مشابه «خشم حماسی» علیه ایران را مطرح کرد، مگر آن که تهران با شرایط آمریکا برای توافق موافقت کند.

سی‌ان‌ان به نقل از چند منبع آگاه گزارش می‌دهد که دولت آمریکا در حال خارج کردن شماری از دیپلمات‌ها و خانواده‌های آنان از کشورهای خاورمیانه است؛ تصمیمی که با افزایش نگرانی‌ها درباره احتمال گسترش جنگ ایران ارتباط دارد.

وزارت خارجه آمریکا تأیید کرده که شمار کارکنان سفارتخانه‌های این کشور در اردن، قطر، امارات متحده عربی و لبنان به‌طور موقت کاهش می‌یابد. این نمایندگی‌ها همچنان باز می‌مانند و وضعیت رسمی فعالیتشان تغییر نکرده است. در عربستان سعودی، دستور خروج کارکنان غیرضروری و اعضای خانواده آنان صادر شده است.

بر اساس این گزارش، وزارت خارجه آمریکا در ماه‌های اخیر شمار کارکنان مجاز در برخی نمایندگی‌های منطقه را افزایش داده بود، اما اکنون بار دیگر ناچار به کاهش حضور آنها شده است.

بسیاری از خانواده‌های دیپلمات‌ها که در ماه‌های نخست جنگ منطقه را ترک کرده بودند، به‌تازگی بازگشته و زندگی خود را از سر گرفته بودند. آنها اکنون مجبورند دوباره محل سکونت، مدرسه فرزندان و برنامه‌های خانوادگی خود را تغییر دهند.

برخی کارکنان وزارت خارجه از اطلاع‌رسانی ناکافی، آشفتگی در تصمیم‌گیری و نامشخص بودن حمایت مالی دولت انتقاد کرده‌اند. انجمن کارکنان خدمات خارجی آمریکا نیز گفته است خانواده‌ها نمی‌دانند برای تأمین هزینه‌های جابه‌جایی و اقامت جدید خود تا چه اندازه کمک دریافت خواهند کرد.

وزارت خارجه در پاسخ اعلام کرده که برای هزینه‌های اقامت، تحصیل فرزندان و جابه‌جایی کارکنان حمایت مالی در نظر گرفته است.

سی‌ان‌ان همچنین گزارش می‌دهد که اسرائیل در روزهای اخیر برای انجام سریع‌تر حملات جدید علیه ایران تلاش کرده، اما تاکنون موفق به جلب موافقت واشنگتن نشده است.

وال‌استریت ژورنال گزارش می‌دهد که پس از محاصره دریایی آمریکا و تشدید تحریم‌های هوایی و بانکی، اکنون برخی مسیرهای تجارت زمینی ایران نیز در حال مسدود شدن است؛ تحولی که می‌تواند فشار اقتصادی بر جمهوری اسلامی را بیش از پیش افزایش دهد.

به نوشته این روزنامه، عراق روز چهارشنبه گذرگاه مرزی چزابه را که دو استان مهم نفت‌خیز ایران و عراق را به یکدیگر متصل می‌کند، بست. مقام‌های عراقی هدف این اقدام را تشدید مبارزه با قاچاق اعلام کرده‌اند.

در پاکستان نیز کامیون‌های ایرانی از عبور از دو گذرگاه مهم گبد و تفتان منع شده‌اند. اسلام‌آباد ابتدا ملاحظات امنیتی را دلیل این محدودیت‌ها عنوان کرد، اما سخنگوی وزارت خارجه پاکستان روز جمعه با اشاره به ضرورت رعایت تحریم‌های بین‌المللی، نشان داد که فشارهای تحریمی نیز در این تصمیم نقش داشته‌اند.

وال‌استریت ژورنال می‌نویسد دولت ترامپ تلاش دارد با همکاری کشورهای همسایه ایران، مسیرهای جایگزینی را که تهران برای دور زدن محاصره دریایی به آنها متکی شده است، محدود کند. اسکات بسنت، وزیر دارایی آمریکا، نیز از همکاری واشنگتن با پاکستان و ترکیه برای محدود کردن مسیرهای تجاری ایران سخن گفته است.

این محدودیت‌ها در شرایطی اعمال می‌شود که تجارت زمینی ایران از ماه‌ها پیش با مشکلات جدی روبه‌رو بوده است. در اواخر سپتامبر حدود ۱۷ هزار کامیون در مرزهای ایران در انتظار عبور بودند و تأخیرها به‌طور متوسط به ۲۰ روز می‌رسید.

توقف محموله‌های کشاورزی و بیش از چهار هزار و ۵۰۰ تن گاز مایع نیز از دیگر پیامدهای اختلال در مرز پاکستان بوده است.

به نوشته این روزنامه، افزایش هزینه حمل‌ونقل و کاهش دسترسی به کالاهای وارداتی، بحران تورم و کاهش قدرت خرید خانوارهای ایرانی را تشدید می‌کند.

این تحولات در حالی رخ می‌دهد که تلاش میانجی‌های منطقه‌ای برای ازسرگیری مذاکرات هسته‌ای هنوز به نتیجه نرسیده و واشنگتن امیدوار است با افزایش فشار اقتصادی و نظامی، تهران را به پذیرش توافق وادار کند.

وال‌استریت ژورنال گزارش می‌دهد که مقام‌های ایرانی در هشدارهای علنی و پیام‌هایی که از طریق میانجی‌های منطقه‌ای منتقل کرده‌اند، گفته‌اند در صورت ازسرگیری حملات آمریکا و اسرائیل، پاسخ ایران دیگر محدود به پایگاه‌های نظامی نخواهد بود و می‌تواند زیرساخت‌های اقتصادی و غیرنظامی کشورهای خلیج فارس را نیز دربرگیرد.

بر اساس این گزارش، فرودگاه‌ها، خطوط لوله نفت، تأسیسات انرژی و حتی کابل‌های اینترنتی زیر دریا از جمله اهداف احتمالی هستند. یدالله جوانی، معاون سیاسی سپاه پاسداران، نیز روز چهارشنبه از امکان قطع کابل‌های اینترنتی زیر تنگه هرمز سخن گفته است.

این روزنامه می‌نویسد با وجود خسارات سنگین به توان موشکی ایران در جریان جنگ، تهران همچنان صدها تا چند هزار موشک بالستیک و ذخایری از پهپاد در اختیار دارد. مقام‌های آمریکایی و منطقه‌ای نیز معتقدند ایران تولید محدود موشک در تأسیسات زیرزمینی را از سر گرفته است.

وال‌استریت ژورنال همچنین گزارش می‌دهد که آمریکا در حال اعزام سومین گروه رزمی ناو هواپیمابر و یک واحد اضافی تفنگداران دریایی به منطقه است و هم‌زمان بخشی از نیروهای خود را از پایگاه‌های آسیب‌پذیر خارج می‌کند.

اظهارات مایک والتز، سفیر آمریکا در سازمان ملل، درباره احتمال ادامه بن‌بست با ایران تا یک سال دیگر، با واکنش دونالد ترامپ روبه‌رو شده است؛ رئیس‌جمهوری که همچنان تأکید می‌کند آمریکا می‌تواند جنگ را به‌سرعت پایان دهد.

والتز در مصاحبه با فایننشال تایمز گفته است آمریکا تا زمانی که با ایران درباره ذخایر اورانیوم با غنای بالا و محدودیت غنی‌سازی داخلی به توافقی معتبر نرسد، به اهداف راهبردی خود دست نخواهد یافت.

او تأکید کرده که نیروی دریایی آمریکا می‌تواند محاصره بنادر ایران را برای آینده قابل پیش‌بینی ادامه دهد و فشار اقتصادی علیه تهران نیز همچنان افزایش خواهد یافت.

در این مصاحبه، هنگامی که خبرنگار از والتز پرسید آیا ممکن است بن‌بست کنونی تا یک سال دیگر ادامه پیدا کند، او پاسخ داد که نمی‌خواهد درباره فرضیه‌ها اظهارنظر کند و ابراز امیدواری کرد ایران پیش از آن وارد مذاکرات جدی شود.

ترامپ روز جمعه در پاسخ به پرسش خبرنگاری درباره همین اظهارات گفت آمریکا قادر است جنگ را خیلی سریع پایان دهد. او اقتصاد ایران را در حال فروپاشی توصیف کرد و گفت واشنگتن می‌تواند تصمیم بگیرد که جمهوری اسلامی را با حملات بیشتر از پا درآورد یا اجازه دهد فشار اقتصادی به تضعیف آن ادامه دهد.

دونالد ترامپ همچنین ادعا کرد آمریکا بر تنگه هرمز تسلط دارد و نفت بیشتری نسبت به پیش از جنگ از این مسیر خارج می‌شود.

در حالی که دونالد ترامپ بار دیگر از احتمال حمله نظامی به ایران سخن گفته است، گزارش‌های تازه رسانه‌های آمریکایی از افزایش نگرانی واشنگتن درباره پیامدهای دور جدید جنگ حکایت دارند.

اکسیوس از یک هشدار اطلاعاتی آمریکا درباره طرح‌های احتمالی ایران برای ترور مقام‌های آمریکایی خبر داده و سی‌ان‌ان گزارش کرده که دولت آمریکا بی‌سروصدا در حال کاهش شمار دیپلمات‌ها و خانواده‌های آنان در چند کشور خاورمیانه است.

وال‌استریت ژورنال در دو گزارش جداگانه از تهدید ایران به حمله به زیرساخت‌های اقتصادی منطقه و تلاش آمریکا برای محدود کردن آخرین مسیرهای تجارت زمینی ایران خبر داده است؛ فشاری که با بسته شدن برخی گذرگاه‌های مرزی عراق و پاکستان شدت گرفته است.

در این میان، سخنان سفیر آمریکا در سازمان ملل درباره احتمال ادامه جنگ تا یک سال دیگر، با تأکید ترامپ بر امکان پایان سریع درگیری، تصویری از ابهام در راهبرد واشنگتن ارائه می‌دهد.

در این مطلب بعضی از مطالب مربوط به جنگ ایران که جمعه در رسانه های آمریکا منتشر شدند،‌ مرور می‌شوند.

اکسیوس به یک یادداشت اطلاعاتی یک‌صفحه‌ای به تاریخ ۲۳ اکتبر دست یافته است که بر اساس آن، دستگاه‌های اطلاعاتی آمریکا معتقدند ایران تلاش‌های خود برای هدف قرار دادن دیپلمات‌ها و مقام‌های آمریکایی در خاورمیانه و دیگر نقاط جهان را به‌شدت افزایش داده است.

در این یادداشت که جی کلیتون، مدیر اطلاعات ملی آمریکا، برای مارکو روبیو، وزیر خارجه، فرستاده، ادعا شده که برخی طرح‌های احتمالی برای کشتن مقام‌های آمریکایی به مراحل پیشرفته رسیده‌اند. با این حال، این سند هویت افراد مورد تهدید، کشورهای مشخص خارج از خاورمیانه یا جزئیات عملیاتی این طرح‌ها را فاش نمی‌کند.

آقای کلیتون همچنین هشدار داده است که اطلاعات موجود درباره این تهدیدها باید در اختیار شمار بیشتری از کارکنان دولت آمریکا قرار گیرد. او پیشنهاد کرده بخشی از اطلاعات حساس با سطح محرمانگی پایین‌تری در اختیار افرادی قرار گیرد که احتمالاً در معرض خطر هستند.

به گفته یک مقام آمریکایی، نگرانی درباره این طرح‌های ادعایی، در کنار افزایش حملات حوثی‌های یمن، از دلایل تصمیم وزارت خارجه برای کاهش حضور کارکنان در سفارتخانه‌های آمریکا در امارات متحده عربی، قطر، اردن و لبنان بوده است.

پیش‌تر نیز به کارکنان غیرضروری و خانواده‌های کارکنان دیپلماتیک آمریکا در عربستان سعودی دستور خروج داده شده بود.

این هشدار در حالی منتشر شده که دونالد ترامپ روز جمعه در یک گردهمایی انتخاباتی در فلوریدا بار دیگر احتمال اجرای عملیاتی مشابه «خشم حماسی» علیه ایران را مطرح کرد، مگر آن که تهران با شرایط آمریکا برای توافق موافقت کند.

سی‌ان‌ان به نقل از چند منبع آگاه گزارش می‌دهد که دولت آمریکا در حال خارج کردن شماری از دیپلمات‌ها و خانواده‌های آنان از کشورهای خاورمیانه است؛ تصمیمی که با افزایش نگرانی‌ها درباره احتمال گسترش جنگ ایران ارتباط دارد.

وزارت خارجه آمریکا تأیید کرده که شمار کارکنان سفارتخانه‌های این کشور در اردن، قطر، امارات متحده عربی و لبنان به‌طور موقت کاهش می‌یابد. این نمایندگی‌ها همچنان باز می‌مانند و وضعیت رسمی فعالیتشان تغییر نکرده است. در عربستان سعودی، دستور خروج کارکنان غیرضروری و اعضای خانواده آنان صادر شده است.

بر اساس این گزارش، وزارت خارجه آمریکا در ماه‌های اخیر شمار کارکنان مجاز در برخی نمایندگی‌های منطقه را افزایش داده بود، اما اکنون بار دیگر ناچار به کاهش حضور آنها شده است.

بسیاری از خانواده‌های دیپلمات‌ها که در ماه‌های نخست جنگ منطقه را ترک کرده بودند، به‌تازگی بازگشته و زندگی خود را از سر گرفته بودند. آنها اکنون مجبورند دوباره محل سکونت، مدرسه فرزندان و برنامه‌های خانوادگی خود را تغییر دهند.

برخی کارکنان وزارت خارجه از اطلاع‌رسانی ناکافی، آشفتگی در تصمیم‌گیری و نامشخص بودن حمایت مالی دولت انتقاد کرده‌اند. انجمن کارکنان خدمات خارجی آمریکا نیز گفته است خانواده‌ها نمی‌دانند برای تأمین هزینه‌های جابه‌جایی و اقامت جدید خود تا چه اندازه کمک دریافت خواهند کرد.

news.title: دور تازه اعتراضات فرانسه؛ ۱۳۵ نفر بازداشت شدند
news.originalSummary:
در فرانسه بار دیگر ده‌ها هزار نفر برای تظاهرات اعتراض‌آمیز به خیابان‌ها آمدند. معترضان در برخی شهرها از جمله پاریس با پلیس درگیر شدند. در جریان این درگیری‌ها ۱۳۵ نفر بازداشت شده‌اند.

news.originalContent:
در فرانسه بار دیگر ده‌ها هزار نفر برای تظاهرات اعتراض‌آمیز به خیابان‌ها آمدند. معترضان در برخی شهرها از جمله پاریس با پلیس درگیر شدند. در جریان این درگیری‌ها ۱۳۵ نفر بازداشت شده‌اند.

وزرات کشور فرانسه گفته است که پلیس در پاریس سلاح و ماسک ضدگازاشک‌آور از معترضان ضبط کرده بود اما اکنون پلیس اعلام کرده که « شهر آرام است.»

تظاهرات امروز پس از شورش‌ها و غارتگری‌های اخیر در شهرهای مختلف فرانسه برگزارشد. ناآرامی‌هایی که هزاران کسب‌وکار را تحت تأثیر قرار داد و به بازداشت بیش از ۲۷۰۰ نفر انجامید.

در آستانه دور تازه‌ای از اعتراضات سراسری که امروز برگزار شد، فرانسه در وضعیت آماده‌باش امنیتی قرار گرفت.

در پاریس، از دست‌اندرکاران یک راهپیمایی‌ که اتحادیه دانش‌آموزی سازمان‌دهی کرده و گروه‌های کارگری از آن حمایت می‌کنند، خواسته شده است که این راهپیمایی در مسیری انجام شود که از مرکز شهر عبور نکند.

با این حال، تدارکات برای مقابله با احتمال بروز ناآرامی در برخی از شناخته‌شده‌ترین نقاط شهر، صرف‌نظر از این محدودیت‌ها، در جریان است.

موزه‌های لوور، اورسه و پیکاسو همگی تعطیل و مسابقه فوتبال برنامه‌ریزی‌شده هم به دوشنبه موکول شد.

برخی کسب‌وکارها هم برای حفاظت از خود، ویترین‌هایشان را با تخته پوشانده‌اند.

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

شهرهای مختلف فرانسه به تازگی شاهد یکی از شدیدترین ناآرامی‌های چند دهه اخیر بود.

محدودیت‌های گسترده‌ای برای برگزاری تجمعات اعتراضی در سراسر فرانسه اعمال شده است، اما همچنان انتظار می‌رود صدها هزار معترض در پاریس و دیگر شهرها گرد هم آیند.

این دومین دور اعتراضاتی است که دانشجویان، اتحادیه‌های کارگری و گروه‌های دیگر مخالف دولت، سازمان‌دهی کرده‌اند.

وزارت کشور فرانسه اعلام کرده است که ۷۰ هزار نیروی پلیس برای تامین امنیت به کار گرفته خواهند شد و حضور نیروهای امنیتی در شهرها را افزایش خواهد داد.

این تصمیم پس از آن اتخاذ شده است که احزاب مخالف، دولت را متهم کردند در پیش‌بینی ابعاد ناآرامی‌های ۱۷ اکتبر ناکام بوده است.

لوران نونز، وزیر کشور فرانسه، گفته است: «اجازه نخواهیم داد هیچ اقدامی بدون پاسخ بماند» و ادامه داده است که  «در برابر خرابکاران، غارتگران و تمام کسانی که مرتکب اعمال خشونت‌آمیز می‌شوند، هیچ‌گونه اغماضی نشان نخواهیم داد.»

او گفته است که علاوه بر اعتراضات برنامه‌ریزی‌شده، پیام‌های متعددی در شبکه‌های اجتماعی منتشر شده که در آن  جریان «چپ افراطی و چپ رادیکال افراطی»  فراخوان به خشونت داده‌اند.

در روزهای اخیر، صدها نفر پس از رسیدگی‌های سریع قضایی به اتهام تخریب اموال، به آتش‌ کشیدن اموال و غارت به زندان محکوم شده‌اند.

نارضایتی در میان افکار عمومی فرانسه بالاست. شهروندان با افزایش هزینه‌های زندگی روبه‌رو هستند و همزمان، هشدارها درباره اینکه هر دولتی در آینده احتمالاً ناگزیر به اعمال کاهش‌های گسترده در هزینه‌های عمومی خواهد بود، به نگرانی افکار عمومی افزوده است.

اعتراضات ابتدا با مطالبه دانش‌آموزان دبیرستانی برای بهبود شرایط مدارس و رفع کمبود نیروی انسانی شروع شد اما در برخی مناطق به خشونت کشیده شد.

امانوئل مکرون، رئیس‌جمهور فرانسه، دیروز و در آستانه اعتراضات تازه با نمایندگان دانش‌آموزان دبیرستانی دیدار کرد.

نمایندگان دانش‌آموزان گفتند آقای مکرون تعهدات روشنی به آنها داده است، اما تأکید کردند که دانش‌آموزان باید «به بسیج و اعتراضات خود ادامه دهند».

مشاوران آقای مکرون به شبکه‌های تلویزیونی فرانسه گفتند که او به دانش‌آموزان اعلام کرده است دولتش از روز دوشنبه مجموعه‌ای از تعهدات را برای بهبود آموزش دبیرستانی اعلام خواهد کرد.

رئیس‌جمهور فرانسه پیش از این  با صدور فرمانی اعلام کرده بود که روز شنبه فقط تظاهراتی اجازه برگزاری خواهند داشت که اتحادیه‌های کارگری به‌رسمیت‌شناخته‌شده آن را سازمان‌دهی کرده باشند. در چند شهر مهم، از جمله لیون، نیس و مون‌پلیه ممنوعیت کامل تجمعات  اعلام شده است.

به نظر می‌رسد اعلام این محدودیت‌ها تأثیر چندانی بر برگزارکنندگان اعتراضات نداشته است چرا که قرار است صدها تجمع بزرگ و کوچک در سراسر فرانسه برگزار شود.

پس از یک هفته که در جریان آن در برخی شهرها مقررات منع رفت‌وآمد به‌صورت محدود اجرا شد، هنوز مشخص نیست مقام‌های محلی تا چه اندازه اجازه برگزاری اعتراضات را خواهند داد.

شهرهای مختلف رویکرد یکسان و سیاست یکدستی در این زمینه نداشته‌اند.

در حالی که برخی شهرداران بر ممنوعیت‌های گسترده پافشاری کرده‌اند، برخی دیگر با برگزاری تظاهراتی که از قبل به اطلاع مقام‌ها رسیده‌اند، موافقت کرده‌اند.

در مارسی، دستور قبلی مبنی بر ممنوعیت تمام اعتراضات به‌سرعت لغو شد تا راهپیمایی سازمان‌دهی‌شده از سوی یک اتحادیه کارگری  برگزار شود.

ناآرامی‌های اخیر در شرایطی رخ داده‌ که فضای سیاسی فرانسه به‌شدت دوقطبی شده است و این کشور خود را برای دوره انتخاباتی‌ آماده می‌کند که ممکن است بیش از هر زمان دیگری در یک نسل گذشته، دچار دو دستگی و غیرقابل پیش‌بینی باشد.

دوره ریاست جمهوری امانوئل مکرون بهار آینده به پایان می‌رسد و نظرسنجی‌ها نشان می‌دهند که نامزد جریان میانه‌روی که او نمایندگی‌شان می‌کند، ممکن است نتواند به دور دوم انتخابات راه پیدا کند.

در چنین شرایطی، احتمالا رأی‌دهندگان فرانسوی باید بین دو حزب راست افراطی و حزب چپ رادیکال  انتخاب کنند.

چهره‌های سرشناس هر دو حزب، آقای مکرون و وزیرانش را مسئول بروز این ناآرامی‌ها دانسته‌اند و می‌کوشند از نارضایتی عمومی بهره ببرند.

دوره ریاست جمهوری امانوئل مکرون بهار آینده به پایان می‌رسد و نظرسنجی‌ها نشان می‌دهند که نامزد جریان میانه‌روی که او نمایندگی‌شان می‌کند، ممکن است نتواند به دور دوم انتخابات راه پیدا کند.

در چنین شرایطی، احتمالا رأی‌دهندگان فرانسوی باید بین دو حزب راست افراطی و حزب چپ رادیکال  انتخاب کنند.

چهره‌های سرشناس هر دو حزب، آقای مکرون و وزیرانش را مسئول بروز این ناآرامی‌ها دانسته‌اند و می‌کوشند از نارضایتی عمومی بهره ببرند.

news.originalContent: The IDF addressed the strikes carried out overnight in southern Lebanon, including in the village of Kfar Reman, saying on Monday afternoon that they began after Hezbollah terrorists launched two explosive drones at Israeli forces on the Ali Taher ridge in southern Lebanon. No IDF troops were injured in the drone launches, and the military said it immediately began striking Hezbollah infrastructure in several areas across southern Lebanon, including what it said was a weapons storage facility.   No IDF troops were injured in the drone launches, and the military said it immediately began striking Hezbollah infrastructure in several areas across southern Lebanon, including what it said was a weapons storage facility. A vehicle in which two people were killed. The Associated Press reported that the vehicle belonged to the Lebanese Scout and Rescue Association, Al-Risala, and that one of those killed was a paramedic with the organization. Two other people were wounded. At the same time, Lebanese reports said a building in Kfar Reman where a large number of people were staying was also struck, killing nine people, including women and children, and wounding 11 others.   Prior to the strikes, steps were taken to mitigate harm to uninvolved individuals, including the use of precise munitions and aerial surveillance," the IDF said in response. "The claim that several uninvolved individuals were harmed as a result of the strikes is being reviewed.” The IDF said that, in addition, following the launch of the explosive drones Sunday, “the IDF struck in the Nabatieh area and eliminated several Hezbollah terrorists. "The IDF will not allow the Hezbollah terrorist organization to harm Israeli civilians or IDF soldiers and will continue to operate to remove threats while remaining committed to the ceasefire agreement." “We lived under constant intimidation because of the bombardments on the outskirts of the village,” Fouad Chakroun, a resident of Kfar Reman told AP as he stood in front of the destroyed building. “Now they have struck the heart of the village.” Another resident, Saleh Madlij, said families and children had been staying in the building. “Are there missiles here?” he said sarcastically. “I will not leave this place.” The BBC reported that, according to Lebanese media, seven additional people were killed in strikes Sunday, while Lebanese President Joseph Aoun warned that the attacks represented a “dangerous escalation” that threatened the ceasefire.

Ministers in the government blame Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the complete neglect of Israel’s public relations: "There’s no leader present it’s been abandoned. A pandemic of sanctions against Israel may break out, and if we don't wake up, it will be too late. Something big needed to be done in terms of public relations, we need to rally the Jewish people and launch an international campaign. There’s no leader to head this. We’re losing. Our friends tell us: we support you, but you’re losing in the court of public opinion." A senior figure in Israel's advocacy efforts added, "They neutralized the Foreign Ministry and took away all its budget. The Foreign Ministry has no funding. To this day, no money was delivered. We’re working with a budget of 2 million shekels allocated for the war since the beginning of the year.  “Each U.S. consulate receives $5,000 a year for public relations efforts, including Independence Day events. For example, the consulate in Boston, which is also responsible for MIT, has to struggle to have such an amount. It’s ridiculous. When you already have a talented spokesman like Eylon Levy, they unjustly suspend him. He was one of the few people who did his mission in the most talented, beautiful, and correct way, and they sent him home,” the source said.   Internal reports from Israeli missions in the United States describe a very harsh picture of Israeli coverage in the American media. One report described, "The media awaited a sign from the government for a policy change, and when it arrived - it unleashed a rampage and published constant harsh criticism against Israel that had always existed. The harsh reports from Gaza, alongside internal tensions in the U.S., threaten to push moderate writers from the mainstream to adopt critical positions toward Israel and demand an immediate and permanent cease-fire.” 'the graphic images undermine the war’s legitimacy' “Pressure on the Biden administration to harden its stance toward Israel and condition military aid for an Israeli policy change constitutes a warning sign for the future,” the report added. “In terms of 'color,' we’re currently in a 'dark orange.' “There’s a change in stances even among staunch supporters of Israel – and while the conservative media fully supported Israel's actions in the past, this time voices questioning the proportionality of Israeli action have also been heard. However, no demand for a cease-fire is expected to appear in those media outlets. Without a fundamental change in the humanitarian issue in Gaza and/or signs on the diplomatic solution on the horizon, criticism of Israel in the media is expected to intensify,” the report read. It was added, "In the last month, the U.S. media’s spotlight turned to the worsening humanitarian crisis in Gaza, with special emphasis given to the suffering of Rafah residents against the backdrop of the possibility of the IDF expanding the ground operation there as well. Leading media outlets flooded screens and front pages with images of starving children, trauma victims, and the destruction of homes and hospitals. Reports and personal stories from Rafah led to empathy toward the Palestinians’ suffering and anger toward Israel's military actions. "Although most media outlets refrained from blaming Israel for creating the crisis intentionally or denying its right to self-defense, opinion pieces sparked fierce debate regarding the proportionality and morality of the ongoing military operation in its current form. Critical voices that were once silenced now have a wider platform.    “Reports focused on the immense humanitarian damages and the harm to innocent civilians, which many analysts argue is unjustified and goes against the values of the IDF’s operation. Even publicists who supported Israel in the past admitted that the graphic images undermine the war’s legitimacy,” the report read. “Against this backdrop, a narrative is emerging among liberal authors, which sees the Biden administration and its policy of providing weapons and diplomatic support to Israel as responsible for the situation, or at least as someone who can bring it to an end." Furthermore, dozens of recent opinion pieces represent a wide range of positions regarding the IDF’s legitimacy, the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, the question of a cease-fire, and the future of U.S.-Israel relations: Conservative media outlets like The Wall Street Journal and The New York Post fully support Israel, advocate for continued military action against Hamas, and refrain from calling for an immediate and prolonged stop to the war.  In contrast, newspapers identified with the center and liberal left, including The New York Times and The Washington Post, criticize the war’s escalation, citing the destructive consequences of the confrontation on Palestinian civilians, and therefore calling for an immediate humanitarian cease-fire, the reports explained.   The reports also expose an erosion of Israel's standing in Washington against the backdrop of the escalation in the Gaza war. This was clearly reflected in U.S. President Joe Biden's statement regarding a "red line" on military operations in Rafah, and Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer's speech.  Most analysts don’t foresee an immediate shift in relations between the countries, but caution against potential political damage to both sides. Furthermore, calls are increasing to use American military aid to Israel as leverage to force policy change in Jerusalem. However, warnings have been raised that the fact of having this discussion could bolster Hamas's position and undermine the chances of a cease-fire.  While conservative media outlets present Israel's policy as legitimate self-defense, liberal media outlets provide a platform for writers who echo the Palestinian narrative, sometimes using rhetoric accusing Israel of "apartheid" and even "genocide." Calls for the U.S. government to distance itself from supporting Israel and reconsider its military aid plan are becoming more common, even in moderate media outlets. The report mentions articles in The Washington Post and The Daily Beast highlighting the effectiveness of pro-Palestinian activists in influencing public opinion in the U.S., especially among progressive Democratic voters. The articles point to growing discontent with the Biden administration's support for Israel, reflected in "Uncommitted" votes in the Democratic primaries and disruptions at party events. Tactics such as demanding a cease-fire and using the term "genocide" have succeeded in keeping the war at the forefront of the national political agenda and increasing pressure on Washington to minimize its support of Israel.  The increasing willingness of Democratic politicians to criticize Israel suggests a shift in the party's traditional stance and leads to speech free of restraint in media outlets as well. This trend reached its zenith with Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer's speech, in which he labeled Netanyahu an "obstacle to peace" and accused him of damaging Israel's international standing, calling for early Israeli elections.

news.originalContent: Rather than celebrating and resting over the three-day holiday, residents of the Jewish community of Hendon in north London and Radlett were struck by shock and grief after the deadly terror attack that took the lives of two daughters of their beloved and esteemed Rabbi Leo Dee, on Friday, the second day of Passover which is considered a holly day in diaspora communities.   Follow Ynetnews on Facebook and Twitter >> Related stories: Israel names two sisters killed in West Bank terror attack At least one dead and six injured in a terror attack in Tel Aviv Family loses two daughters to deadly terror attack Members of the Jewish London community, including friends of the family, who heard of the devastating news after the Shabbat ended, were confronted only then, with the horrific reports of Maia and Rina's death. The funerals for the Dee sisters will be held today at the Kfar Etzion Cemetery.   Rabbi Leo Dee served as the Assistant Rabbi at the Hendon United Synagogue in North London from 2008-2011, and as the Senior Rabbi at Radlett United Synagogue from 2011-2014, after which the family made aliyah. They were a much beloved and respected family in the UK Jewish community. “People feel shock and disappointment. The family were communal people and served their communities well and were well-liked.” said a former member of the congregation at Hendon United Synagogue who did not wish to be named.  “I feel sick seeing this… good people who would never hurt anyone, murdered. I can't imagine his anguish, and pray Lucy survives,” said Joseph, another former congregant.   Chief UK Rabbi Sir Ephraim Mirvis laments the death of the British-Israeli girls murdered in Friday's terror strike on the West Bank.  In a statement, the rabbi said: "No words can describe the depth of our shock and sadness at the heartbreaking news of the murder by terrorists in Israel of Maya & Rina Dee, daughters of Rebbetzen Lucy, who is in a critical condition & Rabbi Leo Dee, my dear colleagues. He continued, “They were much loved in the Hendon and Radlett communities in the UK, as well as in Israel and well beyond.” UK statement not mentioning terrorism The British Board of Deputies also issued a statement expressing shock over the tragic attack: “We are deeply shocked and saddened at the murder by Palestinian terrorists of Maia and Rina Dee, the daughters of Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee formerly of Radlett United Synagogue. We wish Lucy Refuah Shlemah and long life to the family as they cope with this devastating news.” Palestinian terrorist shot and killed 2 British-Israeli nationals, also critically injuring their mother in the West Bank. The victims were identified Saturday as 15-year-old Rina Dee and 20-year-old Maia Dee, the daughters of British-born Rabbi Leo Dee.  While their mother, Lucy (Lea), remains in critical condition fighting for her life, the Jewish community in the UK has expressed shock and sorrow at the brutal act of terrorism against former members of their community.    While many Jewish community leaders spoke out about the attack, the UK government has received criticism from some members of the community for its weakly-worded response to the killing of two of its own citizens.  One member of the Jewish community told Ynet that it was shocking that the UK statement didn’t even mention terrorism. “The response would be different if this happened elsewhere in the world. There is a double standard for British people killed in Israel,” he said.  The UK’s official statement read: “We are saddened to hear about the deaths of two British-Israeli citizens and the serious injuries sustained by a third individual. The UK calls for all parties across the region to de-escalate tensions.” "Tragedy for global Jewish community" Avi Abelow, family friend, said Rabbi Leo and Lucy Dee are beloved and active members of their community in Efrat. "Two of the sweetest people with the sweetest children", he added. "Rabbi Leo continues to teach Torah classes in his Efrat synagogue today. All the youth of Efrat, as their families, are mourning the loss of either their personal friend or the sibling of their personal friend."  He mentioned that "Just last night the whole community got together, including many youth, for a special communal prayer gathering to pray for Lucy's recovery. The brutal Arab Muslim terrorist attack that murdered these two young, innocent Jewish women, and seriously injured their mother fighting for her life, is not just a tragedy for their family, but for the whole Efrat community and the global Jewish community.  "At the same time that another terrorist committed a terror attack in Tel Aviv, which killed an Italian tourist, and terrorist organizations are shooting rockets at Israel from Lebanon, Syria and Gaza, we are once again reminded that the Jewish people have enemies trying to kill us everywhere in our country for just being Jews living in our ancestral homeland.  "If only the UK government and other global bodies would recognize this truth, and truly give support to Israel to stop this ongoing terror war against Israel, which causes loss of life for everyone. In the meantime, as a personal friend and neighbor of the Dee family, my family, neighbors, and community will continue to assist and comfort the Dee family, as we assisted and comforted the family of our other friend and neighbor, Ari Fuld, murdered by terrorists back in 2018."

DALLAS — The day before a game in which he’s set to be the main character, Islanders head coach Pete DeBoer was typically understated regarding his own return here.

“I’ve done this a few times [in] a few different spots,” DeBoer said after the Islanders practiced Saturday. “Your first game back’s always a little special. Just because a lot of people you spend time with and work with and players. So it was a great chapter in my coaching career. I’m now coaching the Islanders and focused on that.”

Some exits are smoother than others, though, even in a profession where you are hired to be fired.

DeBoer’s exit from Texas might be described as memorable for the wrong reasons.

After coaching the Stars to the Western Conference Final for the third time in as many seasons, DeBoer’s club fell behind 3-1 in the series and 2-0 on the Oilers’ first two shots of Game 5, prompting him to shockingly pull star goaltender Jake Oettinger for Casey DeSmith.

The Stars lost anyway. In the game’s immediate aftermath, DeBoer, in essence, tossed Oettinger under the bus.

“We had talked endlessly in this series about trying to play with a lead, and obviously, we were in a 2-0 hole right away,” DeBoer told reporters. “I didn’t take that lightly, and I didn’t blame it all on Jake, but the reality is: If you go back to last year’s playoffs, he’s lost six of seven games to Edmonton. And we gave up two goals on two shots in an elimination game. So it was partly to spark our team and wake them up. And partly knowing that status quo had not been working and that’s a pretty big sample size.”

Less than a week later, the Stars let go of DeBoer.

Having already stated regret about those comments in a September 2025 interview with the NHL’s website, saying he “should have redirected the topic to reflect that this wasn’t about [Oettinger], this was about all of us,” when questions about the goaltender came up, it’s not altogether shocking that DeBoer didn’t want to get into it Saturday.

Did he run into Oettinger when both were in Milan for the Olympic Games last February?

“I did run into Jake and chatted with Jake; yep,” DeBoer said.

Having been out of the league until the Islanders hired him with four games to go last season, that would have been the only immediately obvious opportunity for the two to speak. DeBoer didn’t go into any of that detail, but Oettinger was far from the only one of his former players he ran into while in Italy.

“You’re running into all kinds of players. I had [Marek] Zidlicky, who I coached at the New Jersey Devils; he was coaching with the Czech team. I ran into him in the meal room,” DeBoer said. “I ran into all the Finns, obviously, that I coached in Dallas. We had a big contingent of Finnish players that I really enjoyed working with. So I ran into all of them. Just about everybody.”

With the Islanders, DeBoer so far is thriving. Heading into a three-game trip that begins Sunday against the Stars, the Isles had points in five in a row and looked like a noticeably more detailed team under his tutelage.

“I think right now, you just keep building your game,” Ryan Pulock said. “I think we keep working on all our little details in practice, talking about them daily. You’re starting to see it in game: limiting chances, limiting time spent in our own zone, doing a good job in the neutral [zone].

“We played some skilled, fast teams and we’ve controlled the neutral zone pretty well. I think what he brings in is his structure, his leadership. Everything that he preaches, guys listen. It’s really starting to show in the way we’re playing.”

The woes continue for North Carolina State football.

Seven games into the 2026 season, the program is firing head coach Dave Doeren, the school confirmed.

The ousting comes after the Wolfpack suffered a brutal 31-28 loss to Stanford on Friday, putting them at 3-4 on the year.

“I want to thank Coach Doeren for his service and contributions to NC State, and for always representing the university with pride,” NC State Director of Athletics Boo Corrigan said in a statement. “I appreciate his leadership during his 14-year tenure and the passion he brought to this role.

“We wish Dave, Sara and his family the best in the future.”

Corrigan also revealed that Todd Goebbel, the Wolfpack’s running backs coach/special teams coordinator, will be serving as interim head coach for the remainder of the season.

According to ESPN’s Pete Thamel, former eight-time Pro Bowl NFL quarterback — and Wolfpack alum — Phillip Rivers could be a name to watch as NC State’s head coach next season, with his son, Gunner, committed to play there next season.

Doeren, who still had three years left on his deal at NC State, will be owed a whopping $10.3 million from the school.

Doeren was at the helm of NC State’s football program for 14 years, first being hired by the school ahead of the 2012 season.

During his time at NC State, Doeren finished with a 98-73 record and a 52-57 record in the ACC, posting 10 winning seasons with 11 bowl appearances.

This season, however, has been disappointing for the Wolfpack, as they hold a 1-4 record against Power Four opponents.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

These lefty politicians are sure Fonda her money.

Jane Fonda’s Climate PAC has funneled millions to socialist and far-left candidates ahead of November’s midterms, backing Democrats whose climate and political agendas are as radical as her own.

The actress’ PAC has hauled in $8 million — and injected more than $5 million into congressional, state and local races this year with almost no notice, the group’s latest federal campaign filing for the 2025-2026 election period reveals.

The PAC has spent $1.8 million on operations, handed out $3.4 million, and passed $228,000 to other committees, with another $5 million in the bank.

Once dubbed “Hanoi Jane” for posing atop an anti-aircraft gun during a trip to enemy North Vietnam during the height of the Vietnam War in 1972, Fonda, 88, has been an outspoken social activist for decades who has backed a string of lefty lawmakers.

She got arrested repeatedly in front of the US Capitol in 2019 while helping organize “Fire drill Fridays” to protest in support of the Green New Deal.

Her financial largesse has come in a series of $5,000 PAC contributions to candidates in competitive House races in Pennsylvania, North Carolina and other states — contests that could help determine control of Congress.

Fonda’s PAC also gave $5,000 to Dr. Annie Andrews, the Democratic Senate candidate seeking to unseat appointed Sen. Darline Graham (R-SC) in a closely watched and suddenly competitive race. She cut an ad with her Republican dad who vouched that she is “not some crazy socialist.”

The group has also backed Minnesota Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, whose progressive positions have drawn scrutiny as she faces Republican NFL broadcaster Michele Tafoya.

Fonda’s PAC gave the maximum permitted $5,000 contribution to socialist Wisconsin gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong, whose once-rising campaign floundered as she struggled to explain her earlier call to “cancel Thanksgiving.”

“The Barbarella” star’s group even gave $5,000 to lower-level officeholders like a county commission candidate in Oregon, illustrating how its support reaches beyond high-profile federal races.

Her contributions totaling $40,000 in 2025 in Luzerne County, Pa., home to abandoned coal mines and Superfund sites, helped Democrats seize control of the county council there.

She also gave $5,000 to congressional candidate State Rep. Justin Pearson (D-Tenn.), who was expelled from the Tennessee state House after taking part in a gun control protest on the House floor, only to be later reinstated.

The latest Federal Election Commission filing by Michigan House congressional candidate and Sunrise Movement cofounder William Lawrence shows he also got a $5,000 Fonda PAC contribution. Lawrence’s climate activist group has pushed for sweeping action on climate change. Lawrence was charged with felony trespassing after he locked himself to an Embridge Energy pipeline in 2013 when he was 22.

Lawrence, who says he let his Democratic Socialists of America membership lapse this summer days before he won his primary, is battling GOP Rep. Tom Barrett (D-Mich.) after spending just $700,000 to win his primary. He has been on a fundraising frenzy since, hauling in $3.7 million this election cycle, with donations from other environmental groups as well.

In Oct. 14 Emerson College poll found Lawrence leading Barrett 53% to 45% among likely voters.

Fonda also gave the maximum permitted contribution to the campaign of Sen. Ed Markey (D-Mass.), 80, a co-author of the Green New Deal alongside “squad” Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY). The proposal calls for a transition to 100% clean energy.

Fonda’s PAC says its goal is to “end the stranglehold the fossil fuel industry has on our lives and our planet by electing climate champions at the state and local level.”

Last year, Fonda told the LA Times she admired how Republicans “took over state legislatures” and county councils, adding: “Down ballot, if you come in, especially for primaries, you can really make a difference.” The Post has reached out to the PAC for comment.

Fonda is a canny fundraiser. As The Post reported this spring, billionaire hedge funder Tom Steyer donated $310,000 to her PAC before landing Fonda’s endorsement for his failed campaign for governor.

Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg didn’t hold the trash talk back in his NBA debut.

Lendeborg was tasked with defending Lakers superstar Luka Doncic on Opening Night and the matchup did not disappoint. The Warriors rookie started chirping at Doncic, which continued with back-and-forth banter throughout the game.

“I’m not afraid to talk to nobody. He’s not Michael Jordan,” Lendeborg said.

While Lendeborg wasn’t ashamed by his actions, he added: “I feel like I did kinda take it overboard in the media, but it is what it is.”

He’s not Michael Jordan.”He did admit: “I feel like I did kinda take it overboard in the media, but it is what it is.”On the Boozer matchup: “I always want to have a… pic.twitter.com/sPvnUt5eX5

Lendeborg’s trash talk extended off the court as the forward ranted about Doncic to the media after the Warriors’ season-opening loss.

“Being in there firsthand, just watching all the whining and complaining, I lost all respect, man,” Lendeborg said.

“Like, me getting frustrated, it’s not about the foul getting called. It’s about him complaining the entire game,” Lendeborg added. “Then you get the foul called — congratulations, bro — and you talk to me like you did something great? That’s just weak. It kind of threw me off for a while. Because like I said, I had so much respect for him. Gone, man.”

Lendeborg certainly had his welcome to the NBA moment as Doncic scored a game-high 28 points, seven assists and eight rebounds to give the Lakers a commanding win over Golden State.

But the Warriors rookie is seemingly unfazed by the results.

Things are still heating up between Lindsay Hubbard and Joe Bradley.

“I had a hot MILF summer and I’m having a hot MILF fall,” Hubbard cheekily told Page Six’s “Virtual Reali-Tea” podcast co-hosts Evan Real and Danny Murphy exclusively at Saturday’s Bravo Fan Fest 2026 in Charleston, South Carolina, when asked how things were going with Bradley.

“Joe is hot,” she gushed. “He’s fun.”

Sparks flew between the couple while filming an upcoming crossover between “Summer House” Season 11 and “Below Deck Mediterranean” Season 12.

The crossover featured the “Summer House” cast — including Hubbard — trading the Hamptons for a superyacht off the coast of Greece with the “Below Deck Med” cast — including Bradley.

“We had a great time in Greece,” Hubbard said, adding that she and Bradley also “had a lot of fun in New York” when he came to appear on “Watch What Happens Live” last month.

Real and Murphy also caught up with Hubbard’s ex and “Summer House” co-star Carl Radke at the fan-centric Bravo event over the weekend, getting his reaction to the blossoming relationship.

“I saw their dynamic on the boat,” he recalled of the pair’s meet-cute. “He’s a really good dude. We had a good time.”

As for Bradley’s reputation as “a ladies’ man,” which Hubbard herself pointed out, Radke said, “I don’t watch their show, so I didn’t have any history. So I just kind of assessed what I could see.”

“I was like, ‘I’d ship it,'” he shared.

Radke spilled the tea on Hubbard and Bradley’s romance during a recent appearance on Page Six’s “Virtual Reali-Tea” podcast, when he told us his ex was “already talking to somebody else” and insisted they are better off as friends.

He teased at the time with a smile that Bradley was “quite possibly” who Hubbard had been chatting with, going on to call the maritime hunk “a good-looking man” and “really cool.”

“I know the ladies like him,” he added. “He’s got the ridiculous blue eyes all the ladies love.”

Despite him being career-focused these days, Radke dished that he and Hubbard were “wingman-ing” for each other while filming the highly anticipated crossover.

Prior to Radke spilling the beans, Bradley’s “Below Deck Med” castmate, Captain Sandy Yawn, told Page Six she “felt [a] vibe” between him and Hubbard, which led her to believe there was “some truth” to the relationship rumors swirling about the two.

Bradley has previously been linked to his co-stars Kayley Smith and Victoria “Vee” SanJuan.

Hubbard, meanwhile, was most recently linked romantically to Turner Kafe, the father of her 1-year-old daughter, Gemma. They split shortly after Gemma’s arrival.

Prior to Kafe, Hubbard dated Radke on and off between 2019 and 2023, calling off their engagement.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

UCLA showed up late to its own homecoming.

After looking incredibly flat during the first quarter Saturday afternoon, the ninth-ranked Bruins did exactly what they were supposed to do.

They forced turnovers, ran the ball relentlessly and completed a few big passes on the way to a 28-10 victory over Michigan State at the Rose Bowl.

After spotting the Spartans an early touchdown, UCLA (7-0 overall, 5-0 Big Ten) rolled off 28 consecutive points in finally resembling the dominant team.

The Bruins held Michigan State (2-6, 0-5) to 156 yards of offense, meaning the Spartans nearly managed as much yardage – 112 – on their two fumble recovery returns in the first half as they did running and throwing the ball.

Meanwhile, UCLA’s offense piled up 443 yards after quarterback Ty Dieffenbach returned from a midgame injury scare after apparently getting stepped on.

That was a good thing because it allowed wide receiver Brian Rowe Jr. to haul in a 63-yard touchdown pass from Dieffenbach after beating a defender and reaching out his arms to snag the ball. Running backs Anthony Woods (112 yards rushing and a touchdown) and Wayne Knight (56 yards and a touchdown) did the rest of the heavy lifting for the Bruins offense.

So, why the lifeless start?

Maybe it was the fact that Michigan State was down to its third-string quarterback, a freshman who had never thrown a pass in college.

Maybe it was that the Spartans were down to their fourth-string running back, after the third-stringer had to be helped off the field three plays into the game.

Whatever the reason, UCLA looked like it was taking a win for granted in the game’s early going.

By midway through the third quarter, with their lead up to three touchdowns, that was safe to do.

UCLA avoided a loss that would have been catastrophic to its College Football Playoff hopes while improving to 7-0 for the first time since 2005.

Coach Bob Chesney has also won 18 consecutive regular-season games going back to early September 2025 when he was at James Madison.

After the first quarter went about as poorly as possible for the Bruins – there was a fumble, a holding penalty, a dropped pass and an easy touchdown given up – their defense swung the momentum back in the team’s favor by forcing two turnovers leading to touchdowns.

The first came in the second quarter when defensive back Malik Hartford forced a fumble recovered by linebacker Sammy Omosigho. The Bruins quickly drove for Jaivian Thomas’ 7-yard touchdown run that tied the score at 7-7.

With Michigan State driving in UCLA territory later in the second quarter, linebacker Donavyn Pellot stepped in front of a pass and intercepted it before running 67 yards. The Bruins cashed in five plays later when Knight waited for an opening at the goal line and squirted into the end zone for a 1-yard touchdown run.

The numbers didn’t fully convey the story of how gutsy Dieffenbach was in shaking off a midgame injury.

Already down one quarterback, the Bruins found themselves without another in the final seconds before halftime.

While throwing the ball away under pressure, Dieffenbach got sandwiched between multiple defenders and stayed down for a few minutes. After being attended to for a few minutes before walking gingerly to the sideline.

He returned for the third quarter, with Chesney telling a television reporter that his quarterback got stepped on before his departure.

Dieffenbach completed 18 of 31 passes for 198 yards with 1 touchdown.

The Bruins will play a rare midseason nonconference game next weekend when they host Nevada at the Rose Bowl.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

There can be moments in a playoff series when it feels like a team loses more than just the game.

When a team loses its rhythm, its confidence, its sense of who it is.

Game 3 felt like one of those moments for the Valkyries.

The Atlanta Dream captured back-to-back wins to take a 2-1 lead in the WNBA Finals. The second defeat was even more demoralizing than the first. A 27-point blowout prompted Gabby Williams to immediately deliver an impassioned message to her teammates in a huddle on the floor.

Williams told NBC broadcasters that she didn’t recognize the team. The Valkyries disconnected from the defensive identity that had carried them to this moment.

On Saturday, the Valkyries got back to who they are. They defended with purpose, trusted their teammates and dug deep to outlast the Dream 67-62, which evened the series at two wins apiece.

“The beauty of our sport is as bad as we felt on Wednesday,” Williams said, “we get to turn around and make it right up today.”

Golden State flipped the script on the Dream. The Valkyries converted 18 Atlanta turnovers into 16 points and committed only nine giveaways of their own. They also attempted 18 more field goals than the Dream.

Four Valkyries players finished in double-digit scoring. Williams led the way with 17 points.

Tiffany Hayes scored seven of her 13 points in the fourth quarter to help seal Golden State’s win.

Kiah Stokes had 16 rebounds, including eight offensive boards, and blocked three shots.

Golden State made the Dream work for everything.

For the first time in the series, Angel Reese, a front-runner for Finals MVP through the first three games, didn’t notch a double-double, finishing with only eight points and nine rebounds.

The Dream’s 62 points were their lowest scoring output of the year.

The Valkyries changed their starting lineup, replacing Kayla Thornton and Cecilia Zandalasini with Tiffany Hayes and Kaila Charles.

But that wasn’t Golden State’s biggest adjustment, according to Williams.

“Again, defense,” she said. “I’m sorry if I sound redundant but we just picked up our ball pressure. We’re a bit more connected today and that gives us our energy.”

The Valkyries struggled to impose their will in Games 2 and 3. In those losses, they allowed Atlanta to dictate the pace.

The Valkyries knew they didn’t have to fully reinvent themselves to fight back. They just needed to recover the habits that made them so successful in the first place.

After drifting away from their principles in the past two defeats, Game 4 was a course correction.

“We stopped letting the kind of officiating dictate the game,” Williams said. “Last game, we were very soft. We were expecting a foul call, we were expecting this, but this is the Finals. It’s going to be physical. It’s going to be tough, so we have to woman up.”

Stokes offered some valuable advice earlier in the week after the Valkyries fell into a 2-1 hole.

“The goal when we play on the road… [is] just steal one on the road,” the three-time champion said. “So yeah, we lost on… Wednesday, but to me, that doesn’t mean we’re out of anything, right? Because our goal could still be accomplished if we won today and then we go back home and now it’s the best-of-three series. So for me, it was just shake it off and learn from it and then just get ready because nothing was won or lost in Game 3.”

In what felt like a make-or-break moment, the Valkyries found their way back to who they are. The question now is whether they can stay there.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

A Queens woman had just taken a knife away from her brother who “snapped” and had slashed several other family members when police officers responding to the chaotic scene shot her, the family told The Post.

Shanequa Donovan called 911 after her brother, Rashaun Donovan, 48, allegedly began attacking relatives inside their Jamaica home Friday night, her boyfriend, Edward Grant, said Saturday.

The 38-year-old woman even popped her head out of a window and dropped her keys down to officers to let them into the home on 149th Street in Jamaica when they arrived around 9:45 p.m., cops and family said.

She had managed to grab the knife her brother had been wielding and was still holding it when officers who followed screams to a cramped attic bedroom found her and Grant trying to hold Donovan down, according to Grant.

Police ordered the group to get on the floor, he said.

“She was about to lie down on the ground to put the knife down to put her hands up,” her boyfriend said. “I don’t think she realized she still had the knife in her hand.”

The cop said, “‘She got a knife’ and then ‘Pop! Pop!” Grant, 48, recalled.

Shanequa was shot three times, officials said.

Officers performed life-saving measures on her before she was rushed to Jacobi Medical Center, where she remains in stable condition, police said.

Officials said police officers who arrived had no description of the perpetrator.

The officers identified themselves and demanded that the three put their hands up — prompting the two men to comply.

“The female pointed with her left hand at one of the males across the room, but did not raise her right hand,” NYPD Chief of Patrol Phil Rivera said at a news conference at the scene.

“The female still did not comply and moved in the direction of the officers with a knife in her hand,” Rivera continued. ”She was within several feet of the officers when an officer discharged his firearm, striking her.”

Another officer deployed his taser.

Rivera said police didn’t have reason to believe that the female was responsible for the stabbing.

One of the stabbed men was taken to Jamaica Hospital and the two others were taken to North Shore University Hospital in stable condition.

The shooting was caught on body-worn cameras and is being reviewed by the NYPD’s Force Investigation Division, officials said.

The night from hell had started out normal, Grant told The Post, saying he made tacos for his girlfriend, her brother and two other family members who were home.

“He just kind of snapped,” Grant recalled.

Grant heard a scuffle and went downstairs to see what was going on. That’s when he saw his girlfriend’s brother, Rashaun Donovan, “with two knives in his hand.”

“He was in the living room,” Grant said. “He had the lights off, like waiting to kill us.”

Grant ran back upstairs to the attic bedroom where his girlfriend was and she called police, he said.

“She was frantic,” he recalled. “They probably couldn’t understand what she was saying.”

Karon Davis, 23, who was also in the home at the time of the attack and is the nephew of the alleged attacker, said it “happened out of nowhere.”

“I was immediately the first victim, he broke into my room,” Davis said. “He stabbed me in the shoulder.”

Rashaun Donovan then went up to the attic and broke down the door to get inside, he said. Shanequa pepper-sprayed him.

“She’s screaming ‘He’s going crazy,'” Grant recalled. “He stabbed me. I just started defending myself and my girlfriend. Survival mode.”

Donovan may have lost it because he was supposed to go to a martial arts event in Spain with his parents but missed the flight, Davis said. The couple owns two dojos where Donovan works.

“He was gonna show off for Team USA and all this stuff,” Davis said. “But due to that, I think it was overwhelming pressure…it got to his mental state, and … it just broke him down.”

With one UCLA quarterback already watching in street clothes from the sideline, his replacement went down just before halftime Saturday.

Ty Dieffenbach, who had filled in so capably for Nico Iamaleava over the last few games, got sandwiched between multiple Michigan State defenders and appeared to suffer a lower-body injury.

Dieffenbach walked gingerly off the field at the Rose Bowl before the Bruins punted the ball to the Spartans on the next play.

No. 9 UCLA held a 14-7 halftime lead, scoring 14 consecutive points after Michigan State had taken an early lead.

Dieffenbach had completed 10 of 19 passes for 83 yards while also running 4 times for 14 yards before he went down. He’s been filling in for Iamaleava since Iamaleava suffered a left knee injury just before halftime against Oregon earlier this month.

Iamaleava underwent season-ending surgery this week.

If Dieffenbach is unable to return, the Bruins would turn to Madden Iamaleava, the younger brother of Nico Iamaleava.
