منبع تصویر، BBC / Getty Images

در آستانه دور دوم انتخابات ریاست‌جمهوری برزیل در ۲۵ اکتبر، نظرسنجی‌ها نشان می‌دهند رقابت میان لوئیس ایناسیو لولا دا سیلوا، رئیس‌جمهور چپ‌گرا، و سناتور فلاویو بولسونارو، رقیب راست‌گرای او، بسیار نزدیک است.

در حالی که فساد و جرم و جنایت از موضوعات اصلی کارزار انتخاباتی بوده‌اند، لولا و حامیانش درباره مسئله دیگری نیز نگران‌اند: ادعاهای مربوط به دخالت آمریکا.

آن‌ها مدعی‌اند آمریکا مجموعه‌ای از اقدامات سیاسی، دیپلماتیک و اقتصادی انجام داده که هدفش کمک به سناتور بولسوناروست؛ کسی که به گفته آن‌ها در صورت پیروزی، مواضع مساعدتری نسبت به منافع آمریکا خواهد داشت.

دونالد ترامپ، رئیس‌جمهور آمریکا، گفته است انتخابات پیش‌روی برزیل را «بسیار دقیق» دنبال می‌کند. اما آیا اقدامات آمریکا را می‌توان دخالت در انتخابات دانست؟

منبع تصویر، AFP via Getty Images

در ماه‌های اخیر، روابط برازیلیا و واشنگتن بحرانی شده و دولت برزیل دولت ترامپ را متهم کرده است اقداماتی برای تقویت کارزار سناتور بولسونارو انجام می‌دهد.

از جمله این ادعاها این است که آمریکا آزادی ژائیر بولسونارو، رئیس‌جمهور پیشین، را که اکنون به دلیل برنامه‌ریزی برای کودتا پس از شکست در انتخابات ریاست‌جمهوری ۲۰۲۲ در برابر لولا در حال گذراندن محکومیت ۲۷ ساله است، به‌عنوان یکی از شروط کاهش تعرفه‌های تجاری اعمال‌شده علیه برزیل در سال گذشته مطرح کرده است.

جزئیات این درخواست‌ها در سندی آمده بود که روزنامه برزیلی «او استادو د اس.پائولا» در ۱۷ سپتامبر به دست آورد و منتشر کرد.

طبق این گزارش، در سند نامی از رئیس‌جمهور پیشین برده نشده و به جای آن از عبارت «مخالفان سیاسی» استفاده شده است.

با این حال، هم ترامپ و هم مارکو روبیو، وزیر خارجه آمریکا، پیشتر علنا با زندانی شدن بولسونارو مخالفت کرده بودند.

پروفسور جیمز ان. گرین، متخصص تاریخ سیاسی برزیل در دانشگاه براون آمریکا، به بی‌بی‌سی می‌گوید: «تعرفه‌ها از سوی دولت ترامپ برای تحت فشار قرار دادن دولت برزیل بودند.»

او می‌افزاید: «هیچ توجیه اقتصادی‌ نداشتند. فقط راه دیگری برای دخالت در انتخابات بودند.»

او اشاره می‌کند که هنگام اعمال تعرفه‌ها، واشنگتن در تجارت با برازیلیا تراز تجاری مثبتی داشت.

کارزار انتخاباتی لولا همچنین شرکت فناوری متا را متهم کرده است که میزان دیده شدن محتوای آن را در فیس‌بوک، اینستاگرام و واتس‌اپ، پلتفرم‌هایی با شمار بسیار زیادی کاربر در برزیل، کاهش داده است.

متا این اتهام‌ها را رد کرده، اما ارتباطات داخلی کارکنان این شرکت که روزنامه برزیلی «او استادو د اس.پائولا» به دست آورده، از اعمال محدودیت‌هایی بر حساب‌های مرتبط با نامزد چپ‌گرا حکایت داشته است.

منبع تصویر، Anadolu via Getty Images

۱۹ سپتامبر، روزنامه «او استادو د اس.پائولا» سندی منتشر کرد که در آن آژانس اطلاعات برزیل احتمال دخالت آمریکا در انتخابات را در سطح «بحرانی» ارزیابی کرده بود.

در آمریکا نیز گروهی متشکل از ۳۱ قانون‌گذار حزب دموکرات به رهبری سناتور برنی سندرز، نامه‌ای به روبیو فرستادند و از «تلاشی آشکار برای دخالت در انتخابات برزیل و احتمالا تضعیف آن» انتقاد کردند.

آمریکا دخالت در انتخابات برزیل را رد کرده است.

وزارت خارجه آمریکا در بیانیه‌ای در ماه سپتامبر گفت «هرگونه القای این‌ که نقشه‌ای برای تضعیف انتخابات یک کشور دموکراتیک وجود دارد، دروغی بی‌اساس است».

کاخ سفید نیز در ۲ اکتبر با بیانیه‌ای به امضای آنا کلی، سخنگوی خود، پاسخ داد.

در این بیانیه آمده بود: «رهبران محافظه‌کار در سراسر نیمکره غربی با شایستگی خودشان در انتخابات پیروز می‌شوند، چون همه موفقیت سیاست‌های رئیس‌جمهور ترامپ را می‌بینند.»

«این ادعاها [درباره دخالت] بی‌معنا هستند.»

منبع تصویر، AFP via Getty Images

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

سناتور فلاویو بولسونارو، پسر بزرگ رئیس‌جمهور پیشین، در ماه مه در کاخ سفید پذیرفته شد، اقدامی غیرمعمول برای کسی که رئیس دولت یا حکومت نیست.

او رسما از ترامپ خواست دو سازمان بزرگ جنایی برزیل، پی‌سی‌سی و «کوماندو ورملیو» را در فهرست سازمان‌های تروریستی قرار دهد. موضع سخت‌گیرانه‌تر در برابر جرم و جنایت یکی از وعده‌های اصلی کارزار انتخاباتی سناتور بولسوناروست.

دو روز پس از این دیدار، واشنگتن تصمیم خود برای قرار دادن هر دو گروه در فهرست سیاه را اعلام کرد.

سناتور بولسونارو از این تصمیم استقبال کرد، اما لولا آن را «دخالت خارجی در فرایندهای انتخاباتی» دانست و گفت این اقدام می‌تواند راه را برای مداخله آمریکا در کشور باز کند.

آمریکا در ماه‌های اخیر اقدامات دیپلماتیک دیگری نیز علیه دولت لولا انجام داده است، از جمله تحریم مقام‌های برزیلی مانند الکساندر پادیلیا، وزیر بهداشت، الکساندر دی مورائس، قاضی دیوان عالی، و افسران پلیس فدرال که در تحقیقات مربوط به حامیان بولسونارو نقش داشتند.

واشنگتن در ماه اوت همچنین ویزای ماریا لویزا ویوتی، سفیر برزیل در آمریکا، را لغو کرد، اما گفت دلیل این اقدام تاخیر برزیل در تائید انتصاب سفیر جدید آمریکا در برازیلیا بوده است.

منبع تصویر، Bloomberg via Getty Images

در ماه ژوئن، موسسه نظرسنجی برزیلی «دیتافولا» گزارشی منتشر کرد که نشان می‌داد ۶۵ درصد رای‌دهندگان نسبت به حمایت واشنگتن بی‌تفاوت‌اند و ۱۵ درصد حتی در صورت چنین حمایتی کمتر به نامزد مورد نظر رای خواهند داد.

با این حال، ۱۷ درصد گفتند حمایت ترامپ میل آن‌ها برای رای دادن به آن نامزد را افزایش خواهد داد.

کارشناسانی که بی‌بی‌سی با آن‌ها گفت‌وگو کرده معتقدند رئیس کنونی کاخ سفید نشان داده است که می‌تواند به متحدان سیاسی خود برای عبور از خط پایان کمک کند.

پس از پیروزی ترامپ در انتخابات ریاست‌جمهوری آمریکا در سال ۲۰۱۶، موجی از پیروزی‌های انتخاباتی راست‌گرایان در آمریکای لاتین شکل گرفت، از جمله رسیدن ژائیر بولسونارو به ریاست‌جمهوری برزیل در سال ۲۰۱۸.

همچنین به نظر می‌رسد ترامپ به شکلی بی‌سابقه از نامزدهایی با باورهای سیاسی مشابه خود علنا حمایت می‌کند.

دکتر کریستوفر ساباتینی، کارشناس آمریکای لاتین در اندیشکده روابط بین‌الملل چتم‌هاوس در لندن، به بی‌بی‌سی می‌گوید: «پیش از ترامپ، روسای جمهور آمریکا هرگز تا این اندازه آشکارا از یک حزب یا یک نامزد حمایت جانبدارانه نمی‌کردند.»

او می‌افزاید: «در یک رقابت انتخاباتی نزدیک، چنین حمایتی می‌تواند اهمیت داشته باشد.»

در دو انتخابات ریاست‌جمهوری اخیر آمریکای جنوبی، در پرو و کلمبیا، نامزدهای راست‌گرا و پوپولیست، کیکو فوجیموری و آبلاردو د لا اسپری‌یا، با اختلافی بسیار کم رقبای چپ‌گرای خود را شکست دادند.

ترامپ علنا از هر دو حمایت کرده بود.

در انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای قانون‌گذاری آرژانتین در سال ۲۰۲۵، در زمانی که محبوبیت خاویر میلی در حال کاهش بود، ترامپ اعلام کرد کمک اقتصادی آمریکا به این کشور گرفتار بحران، مشروط به پیروزی متحدش خواهد بود.

ائتلاف میلی با اختلافی بسیار زیاد پیروز شد. نتیجه‌ای که نظرسنجی‌ها پیش‌تر آن را پیش‌بینی نکرده بودند.

ساباتینی می‌گوید: «غیرممکن است بدانیم چند نفر به دلیل حرف‌های ترامپ به ائتلاف میلی رای دادند، اما به نظر می‌رسد روشن باشد که این نوع پیام برای رای‌دهندگان راست‌گرا جذابیت دارد.»

news.originalContent:
Photo by Spencer Platt/Getty Images)

The unholy alliance between the gambling industry and news organizations is growing deeper.

As part of a new sponsorship agreement with the gambling giant DraftKings, local news stations owned by CBS News must air four DraftKings “hits” per day between Oct. 26 and Nov. 3, according to an exclusive report from Status. The deal frustrated some executives, who believed the optics of mixing gambling and news coverage could undermine faith in elections, Status reported. (RELATED: CNN Just Cracked Open Pandora’s Box That’s Worse Than Any Fake News Hoax)

CBS News is not the first media organization to partner with the gambling industry.

In late 2025, CNN announced a partnership with the prediction market company Kalshi. A day later, CNBC announced a similar deal.

“CNBC will incorporate exclusive Kalshi predictions market data into its programs, including ‘Squawk Box’ and ‘Fast Money,’ offering viewers a unique perspective on how event forecasts and probabilities are shifting in real time. A Kalshi ticker will run alongside segments of CNBC’s on-air programming. Kalshi will also launch a CNBC page on its site, featuring CNBC-selected markets,” the network said.

The Associated Press also partnered with Kalshi in March.

“The Associated Press for nearly two centuries has played an essential role in American democracy as the most authoritative source for accurate results on election night,” David Scott, vice president for AP Elections, said. “We’re pleased to be working with Kalshi as we work to expand the reach of AP’s trusted elections data, meeting audiences where they are with reliable information about who voters have chosen to lead their country and communities.” (RELATED: Special Forces Soldier Accused Of Gambling On Maduro Raid Pleads Not Guilty)

Meanwhile, The Wall Street Journal has struck a deal with Kalshi’s competitor, Polymarket.

“We’re making prediction markets data accessible to our users, because it’s a rapidly growing source of real-time insight into collective beliefs about future events,” Almar Latour, CEO of Dow Jones and publisher of The Wall Street Journal, said. “Our mission is to help people make decisions by offering them reliable news, data and analysis. In partnering with Polymarket, we aim to help consumers better interpret market sentiment and assess risk alongside traditional financial indicators.”

Critics argue that because prediction markets allow traders to wager on something as simple as whether a CNN host will say a particular word during a broadcast, the partnership opens up a Pandora’s box of ethical concerns. Reporters and broadcasters, for example, could cover a breaking news event in a way that benefits a wager they made on one of the partnering platforms.

A CBS News spokesman told Status that the sponsorship deal is strictly commercial and will have no effect on its editorial decisions or election coverage.

CBS News is not the first media organization to partner with the gambling industry.

In late 2025, CNN announced a partnership with the prediction market company Kalshi. A day later, CNBC announced a similar deal.

“CNBC will incorporate exclusive Kalshi predictions market data into its programs, including ‘Squawk Box’ and ‘Fast Money,’ offering viewers a unique perspective on how event forecasts and probabilities are shifting in real time. A Kalshi ticker will run alongside segments of CNBC’s on-air programming. Kalshi will also launch a CNBC page on its site, featuring CNBC-selected markets,” the network said.

The Associated Press also partnered with Kalshi in March.

“The Associated Press for nearly two centuries has played an essential role in American democracy as the most authoritative source for accurate results on election night,” David Scott, vice president for AP Elections, said. “We’re pleased to be working with Kalshi as we work to expand the reach of AP’s trusted elections data, meeting audiences where they are with reliable information about who voters have chosen to lead their country and communities.” (RELATED: Special Forces Soldier Accused Of Gambling On Maduro Raid Pleads Not Guilty)

Meanwhile, The Wall Street Journal has struck a deal with Kalshi’s competitor, Polymarket.

“We’re making prediction markets data accessible to our users, because it’s a rapidly growing source of real-time insight into collective beliefs about future events,” Almar Latour, CEO of Dow Jones and publisher of The Wall Street Journal, said. “Our mission is to help people make decisions by offering them reliable news, data and analysis. In partnering with Polymarket, we aim to help consumers better interpret market sentiment and assess risk alongside traditional financial indicators.”

Critics argue that because prediction markets allow traders to wager on something as simple as whether a CNN host will say a particular word during a broadcast, the partnership opens up a Pandora’s box of ethical concerns. Reporters and broadcasters, for example, could cover a breaking news event in a way that benefits a wager they made on one of the partnering platforms.

A CBS News spokesman told Status that the sponsorship deal is strictly commercial and will have no effect on its editorial decisions or election coverage.

news.originalContent:
Photo by SAUL LOEB / AFP via Getty Images

Major U.S. banks moved to restrict third-party artificial intelligence agents from accessing customer accounts Thursday amid growing concerns over the security risks posed by automated financial tools.

Citi and Wells Fargo confirmed restrictions to the Daily Caller News Foundation, citing concerns about unauthorized access to customer accounts. The policies highlight a growing challenge for financial institutions as consumers turn to AI tools capable of accessing sensitive banking information and potentially conducting transactions on their behalf. (RELATED: Political Debanking Ran Rampant At America’s Biggest Banks, Federal Probe Alleges)

“To help safeguard customer accounts and information, we do not permit third-party AI agents or assistants to log into a customer’s account or transact directly within our digital banking platforms,” Citi spokeswoman Gabrielle Baum told the DCNF.

“Customers can, however, continue to authorize limited, read-only access to their account information with certain Citi-approved open banking providers,” Baum added.

Wells Fargo also confirmed it has taken steps to restrict unauthorized access.

“Wells Fargo has taken steps to block unauthorized agents from accessing customer accounts,” a company spokesperson told the DCNF.

You have to be retarded to give AI direct access to your bank accounts. The fact that this technology was invented 10 seconds ago and already so many people are willing to just hand their entire lives over to it and make themselves completely dependent on it and vulnerable to it is so unbelievably depressing but also not shocking.

Major financial institutions, including JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Morgan Stanley and Wells Fargo, are confronting security concerns involving outside AI agents accessing customer accounts, according to an Axios report Thursday. Some agents reportedly appeared to take actions beyond customers’ instructions, according to people familiar with the issue cited in the report.

However, an industry source familiar with the issue told the DCNF that the immediate concern is not AI agents independently infiltrating customer accounts, but customers voluntarily sharing their banking credentials with third-party AI tools.

The source said there is not yet evidence of agents being instructed to perform one task and independently carrying out another. Rather, the activity originates with customers granting access to their accounts, creating potential security risks that banks may struggle to distinguish from legitimate customer activity.

Although customers may authorize AI tools to access their accounts, financial institutions can still prohibit those tools from logging in or conducting transactions.

Unlike conventional chatbots, AI agents are designed to carry out tasks on behalf of users, potentially including reviewing financial information, making purchases or transferring money. Depending on the permissions granted, the technology could move beyond providing financial recommendations to taking actions involving customers’ funds.

Morgan Stanley has begun blocking outside AI agents from accessing its platforms, while JPMorgan, Bank of America and Citi have also restricted access, according to Axios. Banks have tightened restrictions partly over concerns that outside agents could expose customer information or initiate transactions without sufficient safeguards.

AI agents capable of comparing interest rates and moving deposits could eventually challenge traditional banking relationships by making it easier for customers to shift funds between institutions. Such technology could pressure banks’ profitability by helping customers move money out of low-interest accounts, the Financial Times reported in October.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Strapped into a harness, Josh Law was lowered from a US Coast Guard helicopter into the rough Pacific Ocean in the pitch black night, far off the Mexican coast.

The force of the helicopter blades pummeled the water, whipping up spray and turbulence. The Coast Guard rescue swimmer couldn’t hear anything over the noise or see anything in the darkness. Waves of 6 to 8 feet hit him.

All he could do was follow the searchlight from the helicopter with the hope it would lead him to the more than two dozen people flung into the cold waters some 140 miles off the coast of Mexico’s Baja peninsula.

He would personally rescue 16 of them.

“I was experiencing exhaustion at that point,” Law, 24, told The Associated Press in his first interview since the rescue.

“We had very little sleep. But what I was experiencing was nothing compared to what they were at that point … I just had to keep that in mind.”

Over the next two hours in the predawn hours of Oct. 16, Law was the sole person in the water who would get the people whose boat had capsized to safety.

Eleven others were never found.

The Coast Guard called off its search late Sunday.

Law described the dramatic operation to save lives along a remote route frequented by migrant smuggling boats.

What the boat was doing out there and where it originated from are part of a federal investigation.

It was unclear if the vessel got lost, had engine failure, was swept out to sea or meant to go that far. Only pieces of the boat were found.

All who were rescued are Mexican, the Mexican consulate said.

The Coast Guard said US Customs and Border Protection was investigating and interviewing the survivors, but the agency did not respond to multiple inquiries on whether the vessel was a migrant smuggling boat.

The mayday call came in around 1 a.m.

Someone said their boat was sinking in the middle of the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Ensenada, Mexico.

Within minutes, the alarm sounded at the US Coast Guard Air Station in Ventura, northwest of Los Angeles, rousing Law and his colleagues from their sleep.

Helicopter pilot Lt. Miyako Miller checked flying conditions and planned the flight route that would take the crew of four over the vast ocean south of the US border.

Law prepared his dry suit, fins and medical items, then put on a harness that would be hooked onto a cable to lower him down from the aircraft into the ocean.

By 2 a.m., they were taking off from the Coast Guard station in Ventura.

Miller wore night vision goggles to help her fly in the dark. She said she relied on the stars, with no moonlight that night.

As the crew approached the reported location of the sinking, Miller spotted a tiny flicker of light in the distance.

Then she spotted what looked like debris floating in the water, but it was difficult to distinguish what it was. Miller carefully navigated the helicopter over the area, lowering the aircraft until it was hovering about 40 feet above the water.

“I’m doing my best to maintain my references externally by looking outside through the night vision goggles,” Miller said, adding that meanwhile “the flight mechanic is telling me where to position the helicopter.”

Some 250 miles southwest of Ensenada, Mexico, is Guadalupe Island, a biosphere reserve that is well known as a place brimming with great white sharks.

Law said he didn’t think about what was in the water as he hooked himself to a cable and zipped into the ocean, strapped in a harness.

There was no time to waste. While Law’s dry suit provided some warmth, he knew the others had already spent hours in hypothermic temperature waters.

Law said he was guided by a searchlight from the crew, which allowed him to catch a glimpse of the people in the water.

They were scattered across a wide area. Some were wearing life vests that had tiny lights that produced the flicker first spotted by Miller. Others clung onto one another, buoys and pieces of wreckage, shivering and treading water to stay afloat.

Law said he swam to them, flipped them on their backs, put his arm over them and pulled them up using the “buddy tow” technique. Kicking his legs to swim, he carried them to the spot where he could signal the flight mechanic to lower a basket for them to be picked up.

“With one hand, I’m holding the survivor. With the other, I am signaling to the helicopter and working with the device,” he said.

He placed them into the basket, one by one. Then it was hoisted up repeatedly to the helicopter where the crew got each person into the aircraft before lowering the basket again.

Law’s dry suit slowly filled up to his knees with water, feeling like weights pulling on him as he battled heavy waves while swimming back and forth.

With a packed helicopter and dwindling fuel, the crew decided to head to the Coast Guard station in San Diego where ambulances were waiting.

On the flight, Law treated three people with what he described as “bad” wounds, staunching the bleeding. Several of the injuries were “consistent with shark bites” and the Coast Guard provided life-saving first aid, the agency said in a statement Saturday.

Customs and Border Protection officers went to a hospital and said they would process the survivors according to immigration laws after they were medically cleared. Nearly half of those rescued have since been returned to Mexico, US officials said.

Law and his crew returned to Ventura that morning — it was by far the longest rescue operation he had ever done, he said.

The search for the 11 others continued for another two days to no avail. The Coast Guard, alongside Mexico and the US Navy, searched more than 2,441 square miles for a combined 89 hours.

Migrants are increasingly turning to the risky alternative offered by smugglers to travel by sea to avoid heavily guarded land borders. Small boats called pangas leave Baja at night and sometimes travel hundreds of miles north.

news.originalContent:
As Israel heads to the polls on October 27, its polarising and longest-serving prime minister is seeking re-election.

How Netanyahu reshaped Israel after 18 years in power

To his supporters, he is known as “King Bibi”; but to his opponents, he is the king of security failures and corruption.

Disputes over names aside, what is not in question is that Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, has left his mark on the country’s institutions, politics and social attitudes during a decades-long career that has been defined by Israel’s lurch to the right.

As he seeks re-election in Israel’s October 27 polls, analysts say his most enduring domestic legacy may be the right-wing, militaristic opposition that he has helped create and now faces.

Born in 1949, Netanyahu entered Israel’s central political stage in the early 1990s by fuelling anger at possible peace deals with the Palestinians and Syria.

Israeli political leaders have accused him of leading incitement that motivated the 1995 assassination of then-Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin, who was leading negotiations with the Palestine Liberation Organization, by an ultranationalist Israeli. Netanyahu had led rallies in which participants depicted Rabin in a Nazi SS uniform and held signs of him in the crosshairs of a gun, while others shouted “traitor”.

The Likud Party leader denies any responsibility, but former security officials have said they warned Netanyahu before the assassination and asked him to dial down his rhetoric, only for him to refuse, according to Israeli media reports.

In 1996, Netanyahu’s populist tactics succeeded at the ballot box, making him Israel’s youngest prime minister. Netanyahu’s transactional leadership style gave prominence to extreme-right and religious parties that are now an indispensable part of his right-wing alliance.

Under him, religious courts have expanded powers, including over civil and business disputes. State institutions accommodate religious agendas and allocate record levels of funding to ultra-Orthodox schools and institutions.

Netanyahu inscribed his political ideology, especially on the identity of the state and the status of Palestinian citizens of Israel, into law. In 2018, the Knesset passed the so-called Nation-State Basic Law, which states – among other things – that Israel is the exclusive state of the Jewish people and also makes advancing illegal settlements a national priority.

Human rights organisations in Israel petitioned the High Court to stop the legislation from going into effect, but the petition was rejected. International experts and rights groups cite this law, among others, as evidence of Israel committing the crime of apartheid in its treatment of Palestinians.

Netanyahu also re-engineered state institutions, including Israel’s security structures, appointing loyalists and political allies to senior positions. He also clashed with security chiefs that he deemed antagonistic. And in the aftermath of the Hamas-led October 7, 2023 attack, which triggered Israel’s genocidal war against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip, Netanyahu deflected blame and responsibility on the security establishment, prompting Ronen Bar, who was the Shin Bet chief in 2023, to sue him for defamation.

A major change to Israeli institutions that was spearheaded by Netanyahu during his 19 on-and-off years in power affected the judiciary, which is examining lingering corruption charges that could see him serve time in prison if he is convicted. Netanyahu, who is up against three separate cases of corruption filed in 2019, denies any wrongdoing.

Under his leadership, the Knesset adopted legislation that changed the composition of the Judicial Selection Committee to ensure greater political influence for the governing coalition.

Netanyahu called it “judicial reform” to stop what he often calls a “judicial dictatorship” ruling over elected officials.

Opponents called it a “coup” that sparked wide-scale protests: a push to curtail the independence of the High Court and give politicians influence over the courts and ministerial legal advisers.

In line with his efforts to subvert independent oversight, Netanyahu tried repeatedly, but unsuccessfully, to fire the attorney general.

But he succeeded in dismissing the military’s advocate general for leaking a video of Israeli soldiers gang-raping a Palestinian detainee. The soldiers were also released and cleared of charges.

At the same time, Netanyahu is dogged by corruption cases dating back to 2019, which could see him serve time in prison if convicted

The prime minister, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court on charges of war crimes in Gaza, says his work is not over. He promises his supporters he will complete the overhaul of judicial review and press on with other highly controversial policies.

Netanyahu’s supporters and allies view him as a leader who delivers, and one who achieved what others could not. His opponents pledge to undo the damage Netanyahu caused over the past decades, pointing to corruption, social divisions and increasing international isolation as outcomes of his rule.

But undoing such formative changes, many of which are now law, may be easier said than done.

news.originalContent:
Dialysis patients face shorter treatment sessions as severe shortages of fuel, medicines, and oxygen threaten hospitals in besieged Yemeni city.

Taiz, Yemen – It was approaching 10:30am in the dialysis centre of the Republican Hospital in Taiz when a machine began filtering excess fluids, toxins and salts from the blood of Omar Mukhtar Hammoud.

The 16-year-old suffers from kidney failure and is one of 270 patients who regularly receive dialysis at the centre in the government-held city in southwest Yemen. But with essential medical supplies and fuel running critically low under the renewed Houthi siege, doctors fear they may soon be unable to provide the treatment that keeps their patients alive.

Dr Essam Mahyoub Dahan, the centre’s director, warned that a complete shutdown could happen within days.

“Because of the siege and the shortage of diesel and medical solutions, we have recently been forced to reduce dialysis sessions from four hours to just two and a half,” Dahan told Al Jazeera. “We know this is not adequate, but we have no choice if we are to keep the centre operating for as long as possible before it shuts down completely.”

Dahan said the centre’s remaining stocks of specialised dialysis solutions were also close to running out.

The supplies, which are expensive, are normally provided by the Yemeni Ministry of Health every three months. But the latest delivery which was due earlier this month  failed to arrive because of the Houthi siege on Taiz city. It began in the first week of October after Houthi advances in the Taiz countryside.

The city was previously under complete Houthi siege between 2015 and 2016, in the early years of Yemen’s ongoing war.

Across Taiz governorate, where battles are raging between the Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces and Iranian-allied Houthi fighters, the number of patients at risk is far greater.

In an October 12 statement, the governorate’s health office warned that the continued siege and obstruction of essential supplies could endanger the lives of 1,110 patients with kidney failure. They depend on dialysis services in the governorate’s hospitals, which collectively provide about 210 dialysis sessions a day.

International humanitarian and health organisations have issued similar warnings about the impact of the siege on the already fragile healthcare system in Taiz.

On Thursday, Amnesty International called on the Houthis to immediately reopen vital roads into and around the city, warning that the closure of the main road between Taiz and the southern port city of Aden threatened hundreds of thousands of civilians with losing access to food, water and healthcare.

Taiz’s hospitals depend heavily on diesel-powered generators because much of the city’s electricity infrastructure was destroyed during the war that began 11 years ago and has not been restored.

The renewed Houthi siege has severely disrupted the entry of fuel, including the diesel needed to run hospital generators and lifesaving medical equipment.

Dr Shaheed al-Ameri, deputy director-general for technical affairs at the Republican Hospital, said the shortages have had a devastating impact on medical services.

“A very large part of this suffering is because of the shortage of diesel,” he told Al Jazeera. “We have no reserve diesel supplies. Our stocks ran out early in the siege and we are now buying it on the black market almost every day, at prices that have reached five times what they were before the siege.”

Al-Ameri warned that the longer the siege continues, the more prices will rise and the further medical services will deteriorate.

The hospital has already suspended operations in some departments, including essential units, he said.

“If this situation continues much longer, we fear we will reach a complete and comprehensive collapse of healthcare services,” he said.

The shortages are not confined to the Republican Hospital. On October 22, the World Health Organization (WHO) warned that critical shortages of fuel, oxygen, medicines and medical supplies were threatening lifesaving healthcare throughout  Taiz governorate, with some hospital services already disrupted.

According to the WHO, 42 health facilities in Taiz city had reported severe shortages of essential supplies. Hospitals and ambulances require at least 156,000 litres of fuel a month to continue functioning.

The organisation also warned that diesel shortages threaten to disrupt oxygen production, water pumping, vaccine refrigeration and sanitation services, increasing the risks of disease outbreaks, particularly among displaced families and other vulnerable groups.

The United Nations has separately warned that the restrictions on supplies are bringing Taiz’s health system close to collapse and urged the Houthis to allow humanitarian assistance and essential goods to enter without obstruction.

In its October 12 statement, Taiz’s health office warned that continued restrictions on fuel deliveries could lead to the shutdown of medical oxygen production plants, further endangering patients.

Taysir al-Samei, the health office’s media officer, said that would dramatically worsen the crisis.

“Many medical departments depend on oxygen, particularly operating theatres, inpatient wards, intensive care units and incubators for premature babies,” al-Samei said.

“Most hospitals have already suspended services in some units because of the shortage of diesel and the lack of necessary medical solutions, as well as shortages of medical staff who are struggling to get to work because of the lack of transport,” he added.

He warned that if conditions continued to deteriorate at the same pace, some hospitals could stop providing services in the coming days.

At the Republican Hospital, al-Ameri said that shortages were also affecting diagnostics and treatment. The availability of laboratory reagents had fallen to just 10 to 15 percent of previous levels, he said, while approximately half of the medicines normally available were now out of stock.

Prices for the remaining medicines had doubled, he said, placing them further out of reach for patients already struggling with Yemen’s worsening economic crisis.

The continued fighting and shelling around Taiz have increased the number of wounded people requiring emergency care – placing additional pressure on facilities already struggling with shortages of surgical supplies, anaesthetics and intravenous fluids.

Abdul Badi Abdulwuhab, 53, is another dialysis patient in the Republican Hospital, struggling to cope with the shorter dialysis sessions.

His voice was filled with desperation.

“Because of these measures, I suffer from weakness and I cannot bear the pain,” Abdul Badi told Al Jazeera. “Two and a half hours is not enough to remove all the fluids and toxins from my body.”

Dr Dahan said that the patient’s condition had deteriorated since his sessions were shortened.

“These measures are not effective for many patients,” Dahan said. “The only solution is to end the siege and return things to the way they were.”

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

A Florida judge is under fire after she asked a domestic violence suspect for cooking advice during a court appearance — including how to grill the perfect steak.

Broward County Judge Allison Gilman bizarrely discussed what Christopher Johnson would cook for her as he appeared in court for his bond hearing on a domestic battery charge on Monday.

Johnson, who works as a chef in a Florida sports bar, was arrested for allegedly pulling his ex-girlfriend’s hair and punching her in the mouth, leaving her with a busted lip, according to Sunrise police.

“If you were going to cook me a dish, what would it be?” Gilman asked in court footage obtained by WSVN.

“To make food, I’m gonna start with steak on the grill, man,” Johnson replied.

The conversation quickly shifted to the judge’s own struggles at the grill.

“Steak on the grill. Right. See, I either burn it on the outside and then it’s not cooked enough on the inside, or I just overcook it,” Gilman said.

Johnson appeared to offer some advice, gesturing as he explained a technique involving turning the steak between the 10 o’clock and 2 o’clock positions.

“You mean turn the steak?” Gilman asked.

“Ten o’clock, two o’clock,” Johnson repeated.

“Ten o’clock, two o’clock. So you keep it on the same side and you turn it. But are you flipping it? Do you flip it?,” Gilman replied.

The judge had one more question about getting the steak’s texture just right.

“How do you not make a steak chewy? That’s also another — but that’s for another day, I guess,” Gilman said.

The judge set Johnson’s bond at $1,500 and asked if he could afford it, to which he replied, “Yes.”

“Of course you can. With those kinds of things you’re cooking,” she said, adding that she’d “have to” visit where Johnson works for a meal.

Gilman’s baffling exchange with Johnson has since drawn criticism from domestic violence advocates.

Dr. Linda Parker, CEO of organization Women in Distress, criticized the discussion as inappropriate given the allegations.

“Turn the steak? What? We’re talking about steak in a domestic violence case? It just tells survivors, ‘I may not get the justice that I need,’” she told the outlet.

“This is not indicative of how this should look at all and I hope that something gets said to the judge,” Parker added.

Gilman was elected to the Broward County Court bench in 2020 after earning a bachelor’s degree in criminology from Florida State University and a law degree from St. Thomas University, and previously worked as a criminal defense attorney.

Johnson was previously arrested for aggravated battery involving the same woman when she was pregnant with their child, according to court records obtained by WSVN.

He has since been released on bond and was ordered to have no contact with the victim.

The steak talk was not Gilman’s first food-related courtroom exchange, either.

Earlier this month, while presiding over an unrelated case involving a man who said he worked at a seafood restaurant, the judge joked that she was not going to get into her “shrimp-making abilities.”

Hitler’s “Eagle’s Nest” was set ablaze Thursday night after an arsonist torched the infamous mountaintop retreat, authorities said.

Responders first reached the site around 9:52 p.m. to find flames ravaging the notorious tourist landmark, according to Der Spiegel.

More than 200 emergency personnel rushed to the scene, where they arrested an unidentified person of interest.

Police in southern Bavaria later confirmed that a fire broke out at the Eagle’s Nest, which is referred to locally as Kehlsteinhaus.

The perch — which sits at 1,834 meters above sea level — was used by high-ranking Nazi officials during World War II, though Hitler himself visited it only a handful of times.

Eagle’s Nest was constructed in 1938 and to reach the summit, visitors have to ride in a brass elevator inside the rock.

Because the structure sits in such an isolated elevation only accessible by brass elevator or specialized mountain roads, logistics and water transport were extremely difficult, according to Upday News Germany.

Unlike many of the buildings in Obersalzberg, a prominent resort community, the Eagle’s Nest sustained no damage during Allied bombing campaigns.

It was not initially clear if the historic building was entirely destroyed, according to OE24.

The fire remains under criminal probe.

news.originalContent:
Residents and analysts express doubt that October 27 election will bring any meaningful shift in Israel’s policy towards their country.

Beirut, Lebanon – As Israel’s October 27 election nears, so does the possibility that the government that has overseen the invasion and reoccupation of southern Lebanon could be deposed.

But for people in Lebanon, optimism that a change in the Israeli government will bode well for Israel’s neighbours is low.

“I don’t think anything major – or at all – will change for Lebanon even if there’s a change in [Israeli] leadership,” said Beirut resident Fouad Debs.

“Any internal change might lead to small, insignificant changes just to show the outside world that Israeli society and politics are not messed up or evil,” added the lawyer.

For many in Lebanon, Israel’s history of airspace violations, ground invasions and occupation has led to a general atmosphere of distrust, regardless of who is in charge of the country.

“Proof is what people [in Israel] are saying as the elections [approach],” said Karim Safieddine, a Beirut-based nonresident fellow at the Tahrir Institute for Middle East Policy.

“No one is promising withdrawal, and no one is addressing south Lebanon as a crisis or a mistake,” he added, noting that the “general Israeli establishment looks at Lebanon as its prize”.

Israel and the Lebanese Shia group Hezbollah have been fighting, with different levels of intensity, since October 2023 in the wake of the Hamas-led attack in southern Israel and Israel’s genocidal war against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip that followed it. Israel has twice escalated the conflict – first in September 2024 and then in March this year, following the start of the United States-Israeli war on Iran.

In June, following direct negotations that were rejected by Hezbollah, Israel and the Lebanese government signed a US-brokered framework agreement that included the goal of securing the phased withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanon. Still, Israel continues to occupy large parts of its neighbour’s south, where it has systematically demolished homes and infrastructure in dozens of villages, forcing more than one million people from their homes.

Lebanese generally disagree on how to deal with Israel, as shown by a June 2026 survey by Lebanese American University professor Jad Melki and his team.

In the study, 54 percent of Lebanese polled said they supported diplomacy with Israel, while 35 percent preferred armed resistance. But the poll also found that regardless of the tactic, Lebanese views of Israel were overwhelmingly negative, with 87 percent of those polled considering it “as their enemy”.

In next week’s polls, the primary challenge to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu – the man who has overseen Israel’s war on Lebanon that has killed almost 9,000 people since October 2023, including journalists, first responders and children – appears to be Gadi Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar party.

Many Israelis see Eisenkot as a break from Netanyahu, who has been inundated with corruption trials, accusations of failure to prevent a Hamas-led attack in October 2023 and of prioritising attacking Gaza over releasing Israeli captives.

But in Lebanon, the general feeling is that whoever replaces Netanyahu is unlikely to deviate from the current policy of occupation and destruction.

Eisenkot, in particular, is a former general and chief of staff in the Israeli army with a historical impact on Lebanon. He acted as northern front commander in Israel’s 2006 war on Lebanon and is the architect of the Dahiyeh Doctrine, an Israeli military strategy of using disproportionate damage and destruction currently being used by Israel in Gaza and Lebanon.

More recently, he has accused Netanyahu of giving in to US pressure by stopping attacks on Beirut since April, arguing that the Israeli military should attack Hezbollah targets anywhere in Lebanon.

Lebanese analysts said that, although Netanyahu is wanted by the International Criminal Court on charges of war crimes in Gaza, Eisenkot and other challengers have mostly attacked him on domestic issues and from the right, calling him soft on issues of security.

“Those that have come forward as candidates in Israeli elections criticise Netanyahu and his handling of the war,” Elia Ayoub, a Lebanese researcher and podcaster, told Al Jazeera. “They’re not criticising him based on any kind of humanitarianism or anything [related to] human rights.”

Ayoub said the attitude towards Lebanon and other peoples and countries in the region goes beyond the Netanyahu government. He pointed out the governmental and societal backlash to the recent release of NAZA, a documentary made by Israeli journalists in which Israeli soldiers speak about the calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza.

“There’s a profoundly dehumanising discourse that is completely normalised in Israeli society, and the backlash against any pushback is drastic,” said Ayoub. “I don’t necessarily believe that it’s going to change Israeli policy towards Lebanon.”

Since the June trilateral framework agreement, Lebanon appears stuck in a limbo. While active fighting between the two sides has largely stopped, Israel continues its demolition campaign with little opposition. As the occupation becomes increasingly entrenched, many Lebanese fear it could last another generation.

“Definitely, it’s a prolonged situation of neither war nor peace,” said Safieddine. “We’re going to be living in this grey area for a very long time.”

With next week’s election unlikely to bring any meaningful change to Israel’s policies towards Lebanon and the wider region, Ayoub stressed the importance of the midterm polls in the US on November 3.

“The US elections are just as important, if not more important,” he said, “because they tend to determine how much the Israelis feel emboldened toward Palestinians first and foremost, but of course, towards Lebanon as well, and Syria to a large extent.”

But in Lebanon, the general feeling is that whoever replaces Netanyahu is unlikely to deviate from the current policy of occupation and destruction.

Eisenkot, in particular, is a former general and chief of staff in the Israeli army with a historical impact on Lebanon. He acted as northern front commander in Israel’s 2006 war on Lebanon and is the architect of the Dahiyeh Doctrine, an Israeli military strategy of using disproportionate damage and destruction currently being used by Israel in Gaza and Lebanon.

More recently, he has accused Netanyahu of giving in to US pressure by stopping attacks on Beirut since April, arguing that the Israeli military should attack Hezbollah targets anywhere in Lebanon.

Lebanese analysts said that, although Netanyahu is wanted by the International Criminal Court on charges of war crimes in Gaza, Eisenkot and other challengers have mostly attacked him on domestic issues and from the right, calling him soft on issues of security.

“Those that have come forward as candidates in Israeli elections criticise Netanyahu and his handling of the war,” Elia Ayoub, a Lebanese researcher and podcaster, told Al Jazeera. “They’re not criticising him based on any kind of humanitarianism or anything [related to] human rights.”

Ayoub said the attitude towards Lebanon and other peoples and countries in the region goes beyond the Netanyahu government. He pointed out the governmental and societal backlash to the recent release of NAZA, a documentary made by Israeli journalists in which Israeli soldiers speak about the calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza.

“There’s a profoundly dehumanising discourse that is completely normalised in Israeli society, and the backlash against any pushback is drastic,” said Ayoub. “I don’t necessarily believe that it’s going to change Israeli policy towards Lebanon.”

Since the June trilateral framework agreement, Lebanon appears stuck in a limbo. While active fighting between the two sides has largely stopped, Israel continues its demolition campaign with little opposition. As the occupation becomes increasingly entrenched, many Lebanese fear it could last another generation.

“Definitely, it’s a prolonged situation of neither war nor peace,” said Safieddine. “We’re going to be living in this grey area for a very long time.”

With next week’s election unlikely to bring any meaningful change to Israel’s policies towards Lebanon and the wider region, Ayoub stressed the importance of the midterm polls in the US on November 3.

“The US elections are just as important, if not more important,” he said, “because they tend to determine how much the Israelis feel emboldened toward Palestinians first and foremost, but of course, towards Lebanon as well, and Syria to a large extent.”

For a significant chunk of Friday night at Crypto.com Arena, it looked like ghosts of the Lakers’ past – in the form of Clippers forward Rui Hachimura and center Brook Lopez – were going to be the reasons for their first loss.

Especially with their superstar guard Luka Doncic struggling to find an offensive rhythm.

But fellow star guard Austin Reaves showed why the franchise invested the big bucks in him over the summer, providing his team with a spark en route to a 125-117 victory to put the Lakers at 2-0 early in the season.

With the game tied at 64 at halftime, and the Lakers struggling to create separation, taking a small 73-72 lead early in the third, Reaves took matters into his own hands, sparking a 16-4 run that was the difference in the game.

The run started with Reaves converting a tough, physical layup over Isaiah Jackson before assisting Walker Kessler for an alley-oop dunk and Matisse Thybulle on a corner 3-pointer.

From there, Reaves took over, scoring the game’s next nine points to put the Lakers up 89-76 after a pull-up 3 for the team’s largest lead of the game at the time.

Reaves scored 13 points in the third, in addition to 3 assists, for nearly half of his scoring total (28 points).

The Lakers nearly squandered Reaves’ run, allowing the Clippers to cut their lead to 120-113 late in the fourthm but they never relinquished the lead.

Kessler had 22 points, 8 rebounds, 6 blocked shots, 3 steals and 3 steals.

Doncic finished with 23 points (8-of-21 shooting), 7 assists, and 6 rebounds.

Reaves was once again ultra-efficient, shooting 10 of 13 from the field (3 of 5 on 3s, 5 of 6 on free throws) to go with 9 assists for the game.

Lopez had 22 points and 4 rebounds off the bench, while Hachimura had 16 points and 6 rebounds against his former team.

Darius Garland led the Clippers with 26 points and 6 assists.

news.originalContent:

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani sparked outrage Friday when he unveiled a social media video where the socialist shared tips in Spanish on how the public should handle encounters with federal immigration authorities.

“If you encounter ICE, these are your rights,” Mamdani, speaking in Spanish, opens the minute-and-half long video.

The social media-savvy mayor explains that ICE agents “cannot legally enter private spaces without a judicial order,” and tells the public to “look for the words ‘United States District Court’ and the judge’s signature” on the document.

If you encounter ICE, here's what every New Yorker should know. pic.twitter.com/hrjL8JPLyr

He even suggests asking ICE agents to “pass the order under the door.”

Mamdani further adds that people questioned by ICE on the street have the right to remain silent, and suggests they ask, “Am I free to go?” during an encounter and not sign any documents without first consulting a lawyer.

After sharing the city’s legal support hotline, Mamdani concludes the video by noting New Yorkers have “the right to protest” and pledges to “protect that right.”

The video was blasted by Republican lawmakers and conservatives on social media.

“At no point in this video is anyone urged to abide by the laws of the United States,” Sen. Mike Lee (R-Utah) wrote on X. “Because it was not made for the benefit of the people of the United States.”

“Dangerous incitement full of disturbing falsehoods by communist terrorist supporter,” Judicial Watch President Tom Fitton posted. “This statement could put lives in danger.”

Sen. Rick Scott (R-Fla.) called the clip “Unbelievable.”

“The Mayor of New York is openly helping illegal aliens evade [ICE] and undermine the law,” Scott argued. “Radical Democrats are doing EVERYTHING in their power to recreate Biden’s open border disaster.”

Rep. Nick LaLota (R-NY) fumed that Mamdani used “taxpayer resources to instruct illegals, in Spanish, how to evade accountability.”

“Biden’s open border, canceling Remain in Mexico, sanctuary city policies and free hotels, healthcare and lawyers for illegals isn’t compassion,” the congressman argued. “They’re policy choices that are making us more like France and House Democrats are in on it.”

LaLota added, “NYC is becoming more like Paris every day.”

Sen. Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) had a one-word response to the video: “Treason.”

A knife-wielding woman stabbed three people in a rampage through a Queens home Friday night, before being shot down by cops, according to sources.

The apparent home invasion took place at a residence on 149th Street in Jamaica, cops and sources said, as emergency vehicles swarmed the typically quiet suburban street over a report that someone had been stabbed around 10 p.m.

Four people were rushed to Jamaica Hospital, according to authorities at the scene.

The deranged suspect is in critical condition, sources said.

Cops recovered a serrated kitchen knife at the scene.

A family with teenage children lives at the home where the carnage unfolded, a nearby resident told The Post.

A distraught neighbor said she’s “never seen anything like this” in her 30 years living there.

“I went to visit my husband in Long Island in the hospital and came back home and now I can’t get to my house,” 60-year-old Rosie told The Post, who described the situation as “overwhelming.”

“We all know each other on this block and we say hi,” she added.

Police have blocked off the street and the scene remains active.

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Emotions ran high at the Pacers’ home opener in an unexpected way.

The 2025 Eastern Conference champions, who welcomed back Tyrese Haliburton for his first home game since he tore his Achilles during Game 7 of the NBA Finals 16 months ago, found themselves on the receiving end of a dominant Mavericks performance.

But during the contest, as the Mavericks, who won 121-105, continued building a monstrous lead, Pacers wing Aaron Nesmith delivered a hard foul to rising star Cooper Flagg on a dunk attempt shortly before halftime.

Things immediately got chippy after the hard foul as Flagg subsequently went to the locker room with a shoulder injury.

Nesmith was tagged with a flagrant foul, and he also received a double technical foul for his involvement in the subsequent skirmish, as did Mavericks wing Naji Marshall, who inserted himself into the action in defense of his injured teammate.

PACERS-MAVS GET CHIPPY AFTER A FLAGRANT FOUL ON COOPER FLAGG 😳Flagg went to the locker room after the hard foul pic.twitter.com/pQjg9P61KK

Two Mavericks players also appeared to leave the bench though Mavericks head coach Dusty May said he thought both went to check on Flagg, perhaps avoiding any disciplinary action from the league.

“Look, Nesmith is a great guy, a heck of a player. I’ve known him since he was in high school,” said May, who reached two NCAA Final Fours and won last year’s national championship just a few blocks away from Gainbridge Fieldhouse. “Obviously, an unfortunate play. Hopefully, Coop’s fine.”

Flagg continued to nurse his injured shoulder as he walked to the locker room area before the end of the first half and did not return.

May later said Flagg would be evaluated over the next couple of days.

“Cooper has left shoulder soreness, he’ll be evaluated in the next couple of days,” May said before addressing whether Flagg needed an MRI exam. “I really don’t know. I saw him in the locker room, he’s in good spirits. We’ll know in the next couple days what’s next.”

Flagg did not speak to reporters following the game.

With the win, the Mavericks improved to 1-1, dropping Indiana to the same record.

Flagg, who began the season with 32 points in 33 minutes in Houston, finished his two quarters in Indiana with 14 points, six assists, five rebounds and three steals in just 17 minutes.

The Mavericks fly to Dallas and will play the second of a back-to-back on Saturday against the defending Western Conference champion Spurs.

The Pacers head to Brooklyn to take on the Nets on Sunday.

news.originalContent:

The Dodgers didn’t have a number of relievers in the postseason.

The back-to-back World Series champions were swept in the National League Championship Series by Brewers, missing key bullpen staples such as Blake Treinen, Brusdar Graterol, Ben Casparius, Jack Dreyer, and Will Klein.

Will Klein shared a photo of himself in good spirits following his elbow surgery:“All fixed up”Klein is expected to be ready in time for Dodgers Spring Training 🙏 pic.twitter.com/SA3S8dzjid

Klein, who emerged as a World Series hero for the Dodgers in 2025, underwent successful offseason surgery and is expected to be ready for spring training. The reliever shared the news on his Instagram Stories.

Klein sported a 3.67 ERA with 49 strikeouts across 41.2 innings pitched in 2026. The right-hander landed on the injured list in August with right elbow discomfort and missed the remainder of the season because of the injury.

In 2025, Klein became an unlikely hero for the Dodgers in World Series Game 3, the infamous 18-inning thrilled that lasted more than six hours. Klein tossed four scoreless innings, entering in the 15th frame and finishing the game as the Dodgers’ final reliever in the bullpen.

His shutout performance helped the Dodgers defeat the Blue Jays 6-5 in a wild Game 3.

The Dodgers acquired Klein in a minor league trade with the Mariners last June. The reliever is set to be ready for the 2027 season as the Dodgers look to bounce back after an early postseason exit this year.

news.originalContent:
Israeli military raid targets at least 15 towns in the northern West Bank, including Nablus and Jenin.

Israel imposes full closure of occupied West Bank after Hebron shooting kills two soldiers

Israeli forces have raided towns, detaining dozens of Palestinians, hours after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced ordering a full lockdown of the occupied West Bank following an attack in the city of Hebron that killed two Israeli soldiers.

Israeli forces raided at least 15 towns in the northern West Bank, detaining dozens of Palestinians, Al Jazeera correspondents reported on Saturday.

The military raids targeted several northern cities and towns, including Nablus, Jenin, Tubas and Qalqilya.

In Nablus, Israeli forces carried out arrests and raided Palestinian homes in the villages of Jalud and Qaryut. Arrests were also reported in Arrabeh and Burqin, near Jenin, while Israeli forces entered Tubas and the nearby town of Aqqaba.

In the southern occupied West Bank, Israeli bulldozers demolished a three-storey building in Hebron, with families given five minutes to collect their belongings. Israeli forces also ordered hundreds of Palestinian families to forcibly evacuate their homes in the Ein Deir Bahha area of Hebron and its surroundings.

Israeli troops also surrounded the home of one of the suspects in the shooting attack that killed two Israeli soldiers in Hebron, while carrying out raids in the city’s al-Jalda neighbourhood.

The Israeli army said late on Friday that its forces began an operation in Hebron that would last “for several days”, in addition to operations by other forces in “dozens” of areas across the West Bank.

Further east, Israeli forces entered Jericho and the nearby Aqabat Jabr refugee camp.

With the lockdown, nearly 1,000 checkpoints and gates across the West Bank will be closed, affecting millions of Palestinians.

Netanyahu gave the order on Friday, shortly after the Israeli military said it had killed two Palestinian gunmen who attacked a reserve battalion near the Israeli settlement of Telem, killing two soldiers.

Israel’s ambulance service initially reported that at least five Israeli soldiers were injured, two of whom later died.

All Israeli settlements, including Telem, are illegal under international law.

The attack and clampdown came amid heightened tensions across the Palestinian territory as Israeli settlers and soldiers engage in violent pogroms. Attacks on olive harvesters have been rife as aggression has been on the rise before the coming Israeli elections on Tuesday.

Far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir responded to the killing of the Israeli soldiers by calling for Israel to take full control of the West Bank, in which the Israeli government is encouraging the construction of numerous settlements.

Mustafa Barghouti, secretary-general of the Palestinian National Initiative political party, said incitement from far-right Israeli ministers is making the situation worse.

The closure turns every city and village into “a small prison”, with checkpoints and gates blocking healthcare, the economy and education, he told Al Jazeera. He warned that collective punishment “will lead to explosions”.

news.originalContent:
Pete Hegseth says the Pentagon dismantled 80 ‘propaganda cells’ operating under new names at 30 universities.

The United States Department of Defense has designated Confucius Institutes, Chinese-funded cultural centres on university campuses, as a threat to US national security.

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced the move on Friday in a video posted on social media, saying the Pentagon added the organisations to its list of institutions that threaten national security.

Washington has long accused the centres of serving as Chinese propaganda tools and has taken steps to crack down on them.

Hegseth said Confucius Institutes had operated in disguise after being restricted by Congress, calling them “sleeper organisations”.

“It turns out that 80 new propaganda cells across 30 universities had popped up using different names and different charters, but with the same mission: to steal intellectual property and to infiltrate the minds of American students,” he said.

In the video, Hegseth said that Chinese government-backed cultural programmes had infiltrated universities and reappeared in new guises despite congressional restrictions.

Over the past two months, the Pentagon has “systematically dismantled every single one of these organisations”, he said.

The Chinese embassy in Washington did not respond to Reuters’ request for comment.

news.originalContent:
مقام‌های اردن اعلام کردند که در حمله افراد مسلح به مراسم خاکسپاری در کلیسایی در استان کرک در آن کشور، هفت نفر کشته و دست‌کم ۳۴ نفر مجروح شدند.

این حمله روز جمعه ۲۳ اکتبر در منطقه حمود در استان کرک اتفاق افتاد. گزارش‌ها حاکی است که مهاجمان ناشناس با یک خودرو به محل رسیدند، وارد کلیسا شدند و به سوی حاضران تیراندازی کردند و سپس گریختند.

مازن الفرایه، وزیر کشور اردن، در یک نشست خبری مهاجمان را «گروهی از افراط‌گرایان» توصیف کرد و گفت که مقام‌های امنیتی برای شناسایی و بازداشت عاملان حمله تلاش می‌کنند. تاکنون هیچ گروهی مسئولیت این حمله را بر عهده نگرفته است.

ملک عبدالله دوم، پادشاه اردن، نیز اعلام کرد که مقام‌های این کشور با عاملان «اقدام تروریستی در کرک» با شدیدترین مجازات‌ها برخورد خواهند کرد.

تصاویر دوربین‌های مداربسته که صحت آنها تایید شده، ظاهراً سه مرد مسلح را نشان می‌دهد که از خیابان به سوی کلیسا حرکت می‌کنند. دو نفر از آنها ابتدا به ورودی محوطه کلیسا نزدیک می‌شوند و پس از عقب‌نشینی کوتاهی، همراه نفر سوم بازمی‌گردند. به نظر می‌رسد هر سه نفر سلاح کمری در دست دارند.

شاهدان عینی صحنه‌هایی از وحشت و آشفتگی در داخل کلیسا را توصیف کرده‌اند. به گفته آنها، حاضران برای در امان ماندن از تیراندازی خود را زیر نیمکت‌ها انداختند و تلاش کردند از پنجره‌ها فاصله بگیرند. صدای دعا و فریاد در سراسر ساختمان شنیده می‌شد و شماری نیز تلاش می‌کردند از کلیسا فرار کنند.

خالد المدانات، یکی از حاضران در مراسم، به بخش عربی بی‌بی‌سی گفت که حمله حدود ۱۵ دقیقه طول کشید و در تمام این مدت مردم در حالی که تیراندازی ادامه داشت، برای فرار تلاش می‌کردند.

او گفت: «مردم یکدیگر را هل می‌دادند و خود را روی زمین می‌انداختند. بعضی پناه گرفته بودند، بعضی اجساد کشته‌شدگان را در آغوش داشتند، عده‌ای فرزندانشان را محکم گرفته بودند و برخی هم تلاش می‌کردند همراه کودکانشان فرار کنند.»

گزیده‌ای از مهم‌ترین خبرها، گزارش‌های میدانی و گفت‌وگوهای اختصاصی را هر هفته در ایمیل خود دریافت کنید.

به گفته این شاهد، مهاجمان پس از خروج از کلیسا، سوار یک وانت شدند و در حالی که همچنان تیراندازی می‌کردند، از محل گریختند.

یکی دیگر از شاهدان گفت: «صدایی شنیدم که انگار جنگ شروع شده بود. ابتدا فکر کردم اتصال برق است، اما وقتی نگاه کردم، مردم را دیدم که مجروح روی زمین افتاده بودند. صحنه فاجعه‌باری بود.»

وزیر کشور اردن این حمله را «دردناک و وحشتناک» و در تاریخ پادشاهی اردن «بی‌سابقه» توصیف کرده است.

پس از حمله، تدابیر امنیتی در اطراف بیمارستانی در کرک تشدید شد که مجروحان به آن منتقل شده بودند. خانواده‌های قربانیان و مجروحان در فضایی آکنده از خشم و اندوه در اطراف بیمارستان تجمع کردند.

ملک عبدالله دوم نیز برای عیادت از مجروحان به این منطقه رفت.

استان کرک در اردن که اکثریت جمعیت آن مسلمان هستند، جامعه مسیحی قابل‌توجهی دارد. حملاتی از این نوع در اردن کم‌سابقه است، هرچند آن کشور در گذشته شاهد حملات مرگبار بوده است.

جوزف عون، رئیس‌جمهور لبنان، نیز این حمله را محکوم کرد و گفت که حمله به کلیسا «حرمت مرگ و عزاداران مراسم خاکسپاری را نقض کرده و با همه ارزش‌های دینی و انسانی در تضاد است.»

The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders are seeing red after the band My Chemical Romance allegedly fooled fans with lookalikes wearing their signature blue-and-white uniforms during a bloody staged shootout at the group’s sold-out Hollywood Bowl concert.

Pro Silver Star Ltd., the owner of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders (DCC), filed for a temporary restraining order and temporary injunction against My Chemical Romance (MCR) Friday. The legal documents, obtained by the California Post, accused MCR of degrading the DCC brand.

MCR staged “The Black Parade,” a theatrical concert set in a fictional dictatorship featuring pyrotechnics and simulated gun battles at the Hollywood Bowl on October 21, 2026.

During the performance, female dancers dressed in blue and white uniforms, similar to those of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, appeared onstage carrying rifles before being gunned down in a staged shootout, according to the lawsuit filed by attorney Alex Spiro.

“The costumed performers armed themselves with semi-automatic rifles and joined a staged firefight, and were then depicted being shot and crawling off the stage,” according to documents.

The papers claim the stunt fooled concertgoers and social media users into believing the performers were actual Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, sparking online posts that continue to circulate.

“Silver Star does not ask Defendants to change their setlist, narrative, politics, choreography, or even their decision to put gun-toting performers on stage. Silver Star asks only that those performers not wear the DCC Uniform while doing it,” the documents said.

“The universe of alternative costume designs is effectively unlimited,” the filing continued.

DCC’s legal filing also included a side-by-side comparison of an official cheerleader uniform and one worn during the concert, along with social media screenshots of fans who appeared to mistake the performers for real Cowboys cheerleaders.

A cease-and-desist letter was sent to MCR on October 22, and the petition says defendants continued anyway. The documents also mention the DCC uniform is federally registered.

MCR has additional shows coming up at The Hollywood Bowl on Oct. 23, Oct. 24, Oct. 30 and Oct. 31.

My Chemical Romance was contacted by The Post for comment.

It appears that The Nature Boy is going to be OK.

Ric Flair’s daughter, fellow WWE wrestler Charlotte Flair, provided an update on her father’s health after the wrestling legend experienced a scary fall on Friday.

“Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head… (ps: he’s going to be ok),” Charlotte wrote on X Friday evening, referencing her father’s infamous rivalry with The Ultimate Warrior.

Her positive update comes hours after the WWE Hall of Famer “suddenly fell and injured his face” outside a restaurant in Tampa, Fla., TMZ reported.

According to TMZ, Flair got up from the bar at the restaurant and walked across the street without his phone or drink before falling.

Flair, 77, reportedly slashed his head and eye open before leaving in an ambulance.

The ugly fall came shortly after Flair revealed to fans on social media that he was diagnosed with a blood clot in his leg, which caused him to cancel a scheduled appearance at Washington State Horror Con in Seattle.

“Unfortunately, I Am Dealing With A Blood Clot In My Leg, And My Doctors Have Limited My Travel To 3–4 Hours,” Flair wrote in a post on X Friday morning. “Seattle Falls Outside That Range, And As Disappointed As I Am, I Have To Put My Health And Recovery First.

“Blood Clots Are Extremely Serious And Can Be Life-Threatening. We Have Seen This Recently With Jalen Hurts And The Complications Involving Blood Clots In His Lungs. It Is A Reminder That This Is Not Something To Take Lightly, And I Must Follow Medical Advice.”

Flair added that he would be undergoing a procedure to treat the blood clots which he hoped could allow him to resume his traveling.

“I’m Scheduled To Have A Procedure To Strip The Affected Vein, Which My Doctors Expect Will Allow Me To Be Cleared For More Travel Afterward,” he said.

news.originalContent:

Adonai Mitchell may have been dealing with more than a finger injury. It appears he also has a case of amnesia — at least when it comes to the finger on his right hand that has kept him out of action for four games.

The Jets’ No. 2 receiver addressed the media Friday for the first time since sustaining the mystery injury in late September. But Mitchell didn’t recall how he hurt the finger, if an operation was a must as he remained sidelined or any other details regarding the injury.

Text with Brian Costello all season as he brings Sports+ subscribers the latest Jets intel from on the field and off.

“I really can’t even think back that far,” Mitchell said. “I’ve been so focused on what I want to do, which is to be back out there with the guys. That really slipped my mind.”

Asked if he was surprised that he missed so much time, he said: “To be honest with you, I really can’t tell you. I’ve just been so locked in and so ready to get back and help the team. That’s all I’ve been thinking about. That’s all I can think about.”

Most importantly to the Jets, Mitchell is ready to return Sunday against the Dolphins at MetLife Stadium. He practiced fully Friday.

Asked how the finger feels when catching passes, the speedy receiver said: “I feel great, man. I got 10 of them things. I’m just ready to ball with the guys.”

Head coach Aaron Glenn initially listed Mitchell as day to day after he popped up on the injury list Sept. 24. Glenn said Mitchell got his finger caught in a teammate’s jersey. He didn’t play that Sunday against the Lions. A few weeks later, the team acknowledged Mitchell underwent a minor procedure.

Getting Mitchell back will give the Jets their full allotment of pass catchers for the first time since the opening drive of Week 1. Rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. suffered an ankle injury in that game, and didn’t return until last Sunday’s loss to the Patriots, when the first-round pick hauled in six passes for 103 yards and a touchdown.

The offense has struggled to put the ball in the end zone in recent weeks, managing only four touchdowns over the last three games. On the season, the Jets are averaging 18.7 points, the sixth-lowest mark in the league. Over the first two weeks with a healthy Mitchell, they put up a combined 40 points. Mitchell, the Jets’ top deep threat, caught nine passes for 123 yards in those contests.

“I can’t even put into words how excited I am,” Mitchell said. “I think we have all the pieces that we need, and I just can’t wait.”

Said Geno Smith: “With all the playmakers that we have, when you have a guy like AD out there, he can stretch the field, he can be a possession guy, and I think him, Garrett [Wilson], Coop, they just present a lot of different challenges for the defense. And so the more guys, the merrier.”

The 2-4 Jets find themselves at a crucial juncture of the season, with two home games against beatable opponents, the Browns and Raiders. It is a chance for them to get back to .500. Mitchell is eager to make an impact.

“I’m feeling great,” he said. “I just want to help the team, contribute to some W’s. That’s all I’ve been thinking about.”

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

It’s been 12 years since then-Gov. Andrew Cuomo banned fracking in New York — a dozen years in which Southern Tier residents have had to watch their neighbors across the Pennsylvania state line prosper while their own towns rot.

A decade-plus, also, where fracking’s supposed perils have completely failed to prove real anywhere.

If Albany cared about reality, it’d lift the ban and enjoy the ensuing riches.

Instead, folks in Chemung County can only envy those in Bradford County, Pa.

Both sit atop the Marcellus Shale, the largest natural gas field in America.

Bradford has reaped the rich rewards of the fracking boom as companies from around the country exploit Marcellus.

Chemung, which had started to share in the boom, has lost out since 2014.

Bradford County and its municipalities collect over $10 million a year in payments from gas companies; individual landowners earn more in royalties from 1,500 wells.

Subscribe to our daily Post Opinion newsletter!

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Fracking also powers up the local economy: Towanda, Pa., has a median household income of $61,000 and a county poverty rate of 13%.

The figures for Elmira, across the border in New York: $43,000 and 30% in Chemung.

Towanda’s violent crime rate is roughly 60% below the national rate; Elmira’s, 52% above.

High-school graduation rates are 15 points higher in Bradford; Chemung has a vastly higher rate of OD deaths.

So . . . why ban fracking, again?

The prophesied dire side effects — ranging from deadly air pollution and groundwater contamination to, yes, earthquakes — never showed.

There’s not even a carbon-emissions issue: The gas is still coming out of the ground and emitting carbon as it powers the nation — New Yorkers just see zero benefit from it.

Bruce Blakeman’s vow to allow fracking is one big reason he means real hope for New York — and Hochul’s refusal another sign of how hopeless a leader she is.

Chemung, which had started to share in the boom, has lost out since 2014.

Bradford County and its municipalities collect over $10 million a year in payments from gas companies; individual landowners earn more in royalties from 1,500 wells.

Fracking also powers up the local economy: Towanda, Pa., has a median household income of $61,000 and a county poverty rate of 13%.

The figures for Elmira, across the border in New York: $43,000 and 30% in Chemung.

Towanda’s violent crime rate is roughly 60% below the national rate; Elmira’s, 52% above.

High-school graduation rates are 15 points higher in Bradford; Chemung has a vastly higher rate of OD deaths.

So . . . why ban fracking, again?

The prophesied dire side effects — ranging from deadly air pollution and groundwater contamination to, yes, earthquakes — never showed.

There’s not even a carbon-emissions issue: The gas is still coming out of the ground and emitting carbon as it powers the nation — New Yorkers just see zero benefit from it.

Bruce Blakeman’s vow to allow fracking is one big reason he means real hope for New York — and Hochul’s refusal another sign of how hopeless a leader she is.

When the Eaton Fire forced Anne Marie Molina and her family to evacuate their Pasadena home, they had no idea how much it would cost simply to get their lives back.

Anne Marie and her husband, Carlos, had rented the same home for seven years, raising five children there. But when the fires came, they couldn’t find temporary housing large enough for everyone.

Their family was separated. Without renters’ insurance, they found themselves paying for both their regular home and temporary accommodations, draining their savings and maxing out credit cards just to get by.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

That’s why I believe we need to rethink what meaningful disaster recovery looks like.

Even after returning to their damaged home, the expenses continued. Furniture needed replacing. Air filters became essential to protect their children from lingering dust and allergens.

The fire was over, but the financial consequences were not.

Nearly 21 months after the devastating January 2025 wildfires, Anne Marie’s experience illustrates a reality LA cannot afford to overlook: Surviving a disaster and recovering from one are two very different things.

I am executive director of the Jewish Free Loan Association (JFLA), and what has stayed with me most is how quickly people’s lives changed and how overwhelming the financial consequences became.

These were families and small business owners who, just days earlier, were paying their bills, raising their children and running their businesses. Suddenly, they were facing expenses they could never have anticipated.

I remember thinking about how difficult it must be to ask for financial assistance when you’ve always been the person taking care of yourself and your family. Many people who came to us had never imagined they would need an emergency loan.

We tend to measure disasters in acres burned, structures destroyed and lives lost. These figures matter enormously. But they don’t capture the financial aftermath that can quietly unravel a family’s stability long after the headlines fade.

A home doesn’t have to burn down to become uninhabitable. A business doesn’t have to be destroyed to lose its customers. And a family doesn’t have to lose everything to find itself facing impossible financial decisions.

Consider Sissy Keresztes-Fischer, who owns Creo Arthouse, an art gallery and home décor store in Malibu’s Country Mart. Her business survived the Palisades Fire physically intact. Yet mandatory evacuations and the prolonged closure of Pacific Coast Highway contributed to nearly 90% in lost revenues over the following six months.

What surprised me most was how many different financial challenges could arise from a single disaster, including for people whose homes or businesses had not been destroyed. It became clear that a disaster can create a financial crisis even for people who appeared financially secure before it happened.

Following the wildfires, JFLA provided 117 zero-interest, zero-fee loans totaling $1.97 million to affected individuals, families and businesses.

These loans helped cover everything from temporary housing and basic necessities to expenses required to keep small businesses operating.

But the numbers that stay with me most aren’t the dollars distributed. They’re the ones that reveal how long recovery actually takes.

In Oct. 2025, we surveyed wildfire borrowers about their ongoing recovery. Ninety-five percent were still experiencing some form of recovery, with 14% reporting that their situation had actually worsened. Nearly three-quarters were still recovering financially, while 59% reported ongoing emotional or mental strain.

These findings represent a small group of borrowers, but they underscore what we were hearing firsthand: Recovery doesn’t follow a predictable timeline, and the financial and emotional consequences are deeply intertwined.

Emergency shelters, food distribution and immediate financial assistance are indispensable. But recovery cannot be treated as a short-term project with an expiration date. It requires sustained attention to the financial realities survivors face months and years later.

No single nonprofit, government program or charitable initiative can meet every need. Lasting recovery depends on a community willing to remain engaged after the urgency fades.

LA demonstrated extraordinary generosity in the days and weeks following the fires. Neighbors opened their homes. Volunteers delivered meals. Donors stepped forward to help strangers rebuild.

That same spirit is still needed now.

For Anne Marie, a zero-interest loan helped reunite her family under one roof and begin restoring a sense of normalcy. For Sissy, it helped bridge a devastating period of lost business income.

Perhaps the most important lesson I’ve learned is that financial recovery means more than replacing what was lost. It means helping people regain control of their lives, restore their independence, and move forward with dignity.

The fires may be behind us. For many of our neighbors, the recovery is not. And our responsibility to them shouldn’t be, either.

Rachel Grose is executive director of the Jewish Free Loan Association.
